And R. Efraim his son-in-law heard this — and it entered his heart greatly to make a kal vachomer himself — for his father-in-law R. Shmuel mentioned is an elder — and he was young in years — how much more must he fear this — for he too dealt in women's jewelry. And once R. Efraim the son of R. Naftali mentioned was found in the city of Kiev at the fair — for his trade was in gems — and he was engaged in hisbodedus. For he then had in his heart thoughts of repentance — about what he is now occupied with — and is this the purpose? — and for this he came into the world? — and he was standing to the side and weeping. And one of the men of our fellowship asked him why he was weeping — and he answered him. He said to him: "And is here the place to weep? Walk to the house of study and weep there." And Rabbi Efraim mentioned answered him: our holy master said — in the place where thoughts of repentance reach a person — right there in the middle of the market must one do hisbodedus and speak before Hashem, may He be blessed — for by the time one walks to the house of study the thoughts of repentance will have left.

§ 44 — In Lemberg Moharan"as Entered the Professor Rebbe Had Visited; Professor Doesn't Remember — Too Preoccupied All Day; "From This You Can Learn How You Must Long to Hear a Saying from Rebbe" Moharan"as z"l — when he was in Lemberg — entered the professor that our holy master had been at — and wanted to hear some saying that our holy master had spoken there. And he answered him that he does not remember — for he is too preoccupied with his affairs all day. From this one can learn how one must long to hear a saying from our holy master.

segments.he:
לז
פַּעַם אַחַת רָאָה מוֹהֲרַנַ"ת זְצוּקַ"ל אֶת אֶחָד שֶׁיּוֹשֵׁב וְלוֹמֵד אַחַר הַתְּפִלָּה, אֲבָל יֵשׁ לוֹ צַעַר גָּדוֹל מֵהָרְעָבוֹן. וְאָמַר לוֹ מוֹהֲרַנַ"ת, הֶער שׁוֹין אוֹיף הָאבִּין תַּאֲוַת אֲכִילָה (תַּפְסִיק כְּבָר
שֶׁיִּהְיֶה לְךָ תַּאֲוַת אֲכִילָה):
segments.en: § 45 — "A Tzadik Who Dies as a Tzadik — That Is a Wondrous Thing"; "A White Beard and Still a Breslover Chassid!"; The Mishnah of Akavya ben Mehalalel — He Was Greatly Inflamed; "Why Was Rashbi Rashbi — Because He Knew This…"; "From False Grace I Am Clean — My Prayer Is Different, My Learning Different" Once Moharan"as z"l said: A Tzadik az er shtarbt a Tzadik — dos iz davar pele! [A Tzadik who dies a Tzadik — that is a wondrous thing!] Once he said: A vi a vayse bord — un nokh a Breslover Chassid! [Look — a white beard — and still a Breslover Chassid!] And once Moharan"as z"l came to the Mishnah of Akavya ben Mehalalel: "Contemplate three things and you will not come to sin — know from where you came…" — and was greatly and greatly inflamed. And he said in this language: Far vos iz geven Rashb"i Rashb"i — vayl er hot dos gevisṭ. Far vos iz geven der heyliker Ar"i der heyliker Ar"i — vayl er hot gevisṭ. Far vos iz geven der heyliker Baal Shem Tov der heyliker Baal Shem Tov — vayl er hot gevisṭ. Far vos iz geven der heyliker Rabbi der heyliker Rabbi — vayl er hot givisṭ. Far vos bin ikh oykh ikh — vayl ikh veys! [Why was Rashbi Rashbi — because he knew this. Why was the holy Arizal the holy Arizal — because he knew this. Why was the holy Baal Shem Tov the holy Baal Shem Tov — because he knew this. Why was the holy Rebbe the holy Rebbe — because he knew this. And why am I as I am — because I know!] And once Moharan"as z"l said: "Even the true grace that was on the holy Baal Shem Tov and on our holy master — this grace is not found in me. But from false grace I am clean — Un iber dem hitnatstsus eloykus vos iz do in mir — iber dem iz mayn davvenen andersh — un mayn lernen andersh — un mayn esn andersh — un mayn redn mit mentshn iz andersh! [And because of the divine spark that is in me — because of this my prayer is different — and my learning different — and my eating different — and my speech with people is different!]

segments.he:
לח
ר' יִצְחָק מִנָאוִויגְרֶעבְּלִי נָתַן לְאֶחָד סִפְרֵי רַבֵּנוּ זְצוּקַ"ל, וְנֶהֱנָה מֵהֶם מְאֹד וְנָתַן פְּרִישַׂת שָׁלוֹם לְר' נָתָן. אָמַר אֶחָד מֵאַנְשֵׁי שְׁלוֹמֵנוּ לְהָר' נָתָן אֲבָל הָאִישׁ הַנַּ"ל מִסְתַּכֵּל בְּכָל הַסְּפָרִים. אָמַר מוֹהֲרַנַ"ת לְר' אִיצִיֶא, דּוּא זָאלְסְט אִין זַיינֶע אַרְבַּע אַמּוֹת נִיט שְׁטֵיְין (שֶׁלֹּא תַּעֲמוֹד בְּאַרְבַּע אַמוֹתָיו):
segments.en: § 46 — Story of the Spirits Under the Pillow — Ask If Mashiach Came, Drink Spirits, Go Back to Sleep; Moharan"as: "That's No Advice — Put Psalms Under Your Head — and When You Wake, Cry Afresh from the Depths" Once they told before Moharan"as z"l: what Chassidim are accustomed to do — they put intoxicating drink under their pillow — and when they wake from sleep they ask: has Mashiach not yet come? — and drink the intoxicating drink and get drunk and go back to sleep. For they say: as long as Mashiach has not come — one must put the evil inclination to sleep — Men darf farshloyfn dem yetser hore! [One must put the evil inclination to sleep!] For during sleep it is impossible to sin. And Moharan"as z"l said to them: this is no advice. Rather one must put Psalms under one's head — and when one wakes from sleep — if Mashiach has not come — one must cry out afresh from the depths of one's heart — Lodz tfilem! [Say Psalms!]

segments.he:
לט
פַּעַם אַחַת אָמַר מוֹהֲרַנַ"ת עַל נֶכְדֵי רַבִּי פִּינְחָס מִקָּארִיץ זַ"ל שֶׁנִּתְחַיְּבוּ מַלְקוֹת עַל שֶׁהָיָה בְּיָדָם לִמְחוֹת וְלֹא מִחוּ. אַף־עַל־פִּי־כֵן הֶחֱזִיקוּ יָדָם עִם אַנְשֵׁי שְׁלוֹמֵנוּ, וּפַעַם אַחַת הָיָה ר' פִּינְחָס נֶכֶד הָרַב ר' פִּינְחָס מִקָּארִיץ עַל בְּרִית מִילָה עִם ר' מֵאִיר מִטֶּעפְּלִיק, וְנֶהֱנָה מְאֹד מֵהַבְּרָכָה שֶׁבֵּרַךְ עַל הַמִּילָה, שֶׁהַר' מֵאִיר הַנַּ"ל הָיָה מוֹהֵל, וְשִׁבַּח אֶת אַנְשֵׁי שְׁלוֹמֵנוּ. וְשָׁם הָיָה אֶחָד שֶׁדִּבֵּר עַל רַבֵּנוּ זְצוּקַ"ל, וְהֻכְרַח לְקַבֵּל נְזִיפָה לִפְנֵי ר' פִּינְחָס הַנַּ"ל. וְשָׁאֲלוּ אוֹתוֹ הֲלֹא יֵשׁ הַעְתָּקָה מִמְפֻרְסָם אֶחָד, וְהֵשִׁיב לָהֶם הָר' פִּינְחָס, הַעְתָּקָה מֵהַעְתָּקָה שְׁטֶעלְט אִיהְר אַקֶעגִין, קֶעגִין לִקּוּטֵי מוֹהֲרַ"ן (הַעְתָּקָה מֵהַעְתָּקָה אַתֶּם מַעֲמִידִים נֶגֶד, נֶגֶד לִקּוּטֵי מוֹהֲרַ"ן):
segments.en: §§ 47–48 — R. Meir of Teplik — Great Close One of Moharan"as; Service Not Going in Order; "As Long as Mashiach Has Not Come — One Must Keep Pulling"; He Merited Ordered Service in Old Age — Because of His Hisbodedus in Youth; Rebbe's Blessing That When He Lay Down He Fell Asleep Immediately; A Famous One Prayed in Secret; "Let Them Toil in Prayer as I Toil"; Torah §15 of Or HaGanuz — Meaning: Whoever Wants to Taste Rebbe's Light Must Increase Hisbodedus R. Meir of Teplik was among the greatest of those close to Moharan"as z"l. And his way was to complain before Moharan"as z"l that service was not going in order with him — and he would strengthen him. Once he came before him and said that for some time the service has been going in order with him. Moharan"as said to him in this language: Ikh veys nit — efsher iz dir gut — un ikh veys az kol zman Mashiakh iz nokh nit gekumen — darf men halṭn in eyn raysn! [I don't know — perhaps it is good with you — but I know that as long as Mashiakh has not yet come — one must keep pulling and pulling!] Moharan"as z"l said: why did I merit that in old age the service goes in order with me? — because I had much hisbodedus in my youth. Moharan"as z"l had a blessing from our master z"l — that when he laid himself down to sleep he would immediately fall asleep. Once they told before Moharan"as about a famous one who prayed secretly — and Moharan"as was stirred and said: they compare themselves to our holy master — by him it was fulfilled: "oil in secret" [shemen bakhasha'i] as explained in Torah §21. And he said in this language: Zoln zey zikh azoy mutshn un davvenen azoy vi ikh mutshe zikh! [Let them toil themselves in prayer as I toil myself!] Once Moharan"as z"l said before the men of our fellowship the Torah §15 of Or HaGanuz — beginning in this language: "Whoever wants to taste the taste of the Or HaGanuz etc. must engage in the aspect of judgment which is hisbodedus." And when he finished the Torah — some people left and only the men of our fellowship remained. He answered and said to them: the explanation of the Torah is thus — whoever wants to taste the light of our holy master — which is the Or HaGanuz — must increase hisbodedus.

segments.he:
מ
אֶחָד מֵאַנְשֵׁי שְׁלוֹמֵנוּ לֹא הָיָה רוֹצֶה לֵילֵךְ אֶל הַשָּׁלֹשׁ סְעֻדּוֹת שֶׁל הָר' נָתָן, כִּי מוֹהֲרַנַ"ת הָיָה רָגִיל לְדַבֵּר עִם אַנְשֵׁי שְׁלוֹמֵנוּ מִיִּרְאַת שָׁמַיִם, אַךְ בְּשָׁלֹשׁ סְעֻדּוֹת לֹא הָיָה רוֹצֶה, כִּי לֹא רָצָה לְהַנְהִיג רַבָּנוּת. פַּעַם אַחַת בָּא הָאִישׁ הַנַּ"ל לְמוֹהֲרַנַ"ת וְרָאָה כְּתַב־יָד שֶׁל מוֹהֲרַנַ"ת כִּי מוֹהֲרַנַ"ת כָּתַב חֲלוֹמוֹתָיו, וְכָתַב שֶׁפַּעַם אֶחָד חָלַם לוֹ שֶׁבָּא רַבֵּנוּ זְצוּקַ"ל אֵלָיו, וְהוֹכִיחַ אוֹתוֹ עַל שֶׁמְּרַחֵק אֲנָשִׁים מֵאִתּוֹ, אָז אָמַר הָאִישׁ שֶׁמֵּהַיּוֹם בְּוַדַּאי יֵשֵׁב מוֹהֲרַנַ"ת בְּשָׁלֹשׁ סְעֻדּוֹת:
segments.en: § 49 — Wife of Moharan"as Passed Away During the Conscription Decree; R. Yitzchak His Son — Wife Refused Him; Moharan"as Cried Out "He Is Murdering My Child!"; R. Nathan's Brother Leybush Made Peace With His Wife; The Man With the Bad Wife — Pray Specifically for Half a Year The wife of Moharan"as passed away at the time of the conscription of young Jews into the Czar's Russian army — and she died from the anguish of that. And Moharan"as said about this: one must weep over this like over the aforementioned decree. R. Yitzchak his son — Moharan"as was marrying him off in Tcherkaz [Cherkasy] — and after the wedding his wife refused him [did not want to live with him] [did not want to live with him] — and his father-in-law loved him greatly and did not want to let him go. And he thought in his mind: now she is young and does not have full understanding — and because of this she refuses him — and if he waits a year or more she will have more understanding and perhaps she will agree. And Moharan"as z"l came and said to his father-in-law that he should choose what he wants — either she should live with him — or if not — there should be a get [divorce]. And he answered him as mentioned — that he should wait some years until she grows up and has more understanding — for a get his father-in-law did not want since he loved him greatly — and to live with him she did not want. And when Moharan"as z"l saw there was no advice — he went out and grabbed the hairs of his head and cried out in a great voice: Givald! Er koylit mayn kind! [Help! He is murdering my child!] Until some people gathered — and they intervened that there should be a get. And once there was the matter that R. Nathan had a brother named Leybush — and he had a small quarrel with his wife for a time and separated from her. And afterwards she returned and was persuaded and agreed — and peace was made with her. And then Moharan"as z"l said: this that he returned and made peace with her — this was brought about through the power of the true Tzadik — who has the power to transform hatred to will. And once in the days of Moharan"as z"l there was one who married a bad wife — even bad to others — and after the marriage it became known to him — and he did not know what to do for she greatly aggravated him. And he asked Moharan"as z"l for advice what to do — and he answered him with the advice that he should pray specifically every day for half a year for an hour — namely that she should be somewhat better to him and not so bad etc.

segments.he:
מא
פַּעַם אַחַת נָסַע הָר' נַחְמָן מִטּוּלְטְשִׁין עִם מוֹהֲרַנַ"ת זְצוּקַ"ל בַּדֶּרֶךְ, וְהוֹכִיחַ אוֹתוֹ עַל שֶׁאֵינוֹ לוֹמֵד. וּכְשֶׁבָּאוּ לְאַכְסַנְיָא לָקַח הָר' נַחְמָן גְּמָרָא וְהִתְחִיל לִלְמֹד. אָמַר לוֹ מוֹהֲרַנַ"ת דָּאס הֵייסְט בֵּייזֶער לַמְדָן, דֶּער בַּעַל שֵׁם טוֹב הָאט גִּיזָאגְט דָּאס עֶר אִיז גֶּעקוּמֶען אוֹיף דֶּער וֶועלְט אוֹיְס רַיְיסֶען דֶּעם בֵּייזֶען לַמְדָן (זֶה נִקְרָא לַמְדָן־כָּעוּס, הַבַּעַל שֵׁם טוֹב אָמַר שֶׁהוּא בָּא לָעוֹלָם לַעֲקוֹר אֶת עִנְיָן הַלַּמְדָן־ כָּעוּס), וְאָמַר אֵלָיו, אֶלָּא תִּלְמֹד חֻמָּשׁ, מִשְׁנָיוֹת, עֵין יַעֲקֹב, שֻׁלְחָן עָרוּךְ, מִדְרָשׁ וְכַדּוֹמֶה כָּל הַדְּבָרִים הַקְּטַנִּים. כִּי הָר' נַחְמָן נִתְקָרֵב לְמוֹהֲרַנַ"ת בֶּן עֶשְׂרִים שָׁנָה, וְלֹא הָיָה אָז בֶּן־תּוֹרָה, וְאִם הָיָה לוֹמֵד גְּמָרָא הָיָה נִשְׁאָר בְּלַמְדָן וְלֹא בְּצַדִּיק, עַל־כֵּן הֵבִין מוֹהֲרַנַ"ת כִּי אִי אֶפְשָׁר שֶׁיִּלְמֹד גְּמָרָא גַּם־כֵּן. עַל־כֵּן הִרְגִּיל אוֹתוֹ בִּדְבָרִים קְטַנִּים, וּמִזֶּה נַעֲשָׂה גָּדוֹל וְכוּ'. וּפַעַם אַחַת אָמַר מוֹהֲרַנַ"ת אֲנִי גַּם־כֵּן רְצוֹנִי לְהִתְפַּלֵּל כְּוָתִיקִין אֲבָל לֹא בְּבֵיְיזִין־לַמְדָן. כִּי חָמִיו הָיָה רָגִיל לְהִתְפַּלֵּל וָתִיקִין, וְהָיָה מְקַצֵּר בַּתְּפִלָּה כְּדֵי לִפְגֹּעַ הַנֵּץ:
segments.en:
§ 50 — "How Is It Possible That This World Exists When There Is the Known Desire in the World?" Once Moharan"as said: "How is it possible that this world exists when there is the known desire in the world?"

§ 51 — "I Don't Say People Will Be Punished for Not Being a Breslover Chassid — Rather They Will Be Punished for Their Flaws; If You Had Been a Breslover Chassid You Would Not Have Had These Flaws" Once someone said to Moharan"as: people say of you that you say people will be punished — Me'vet shmaysn oyf vos nit geven a Breslover Chassid! [One will be punished for not having been a Breslover Chassid!] And he said to him: I do not say this. Rather: they will be punished for their flaws. If you see your great flaws and understand — had you been a Breslover Chassid — you would not have had these flaws.

segments.he:
מב
אָמַר מוֹהֲרַנַ"ת שֶׁאֲנָשִׁים כְּשֵׁרִים הָיוּ אוֹמְרִים שֶׁבֵּין הַמְּצָרִים יֵשׁ לָהֶם יְרִידָה:
segments.en: § 52 — Halachos Matanah §4 "Vayetse Yaakov" — Said on Shabbos Morning After Washing Hands; He Said It Until It Was Almost Evening; Almost Did Not Eat the Third Meal Halachos Matanah [Laws of Gifts], §4 — "And Yaakov went out" [Vayetse Yaakov] — was said on Shabbos morning after he washed his hands to eat the morning meal. He began to say it until it was almost evening — and they almost did not eat the third meal.

segments.he:
מג
מוֹהֲרַנַ"ת אָמַר לְאֶחָד מֵאַנְשֵׁי שְׁלוֹמֵנוּ, בְּחָנוּנִי נָא בָּזֹאת, אִם יִהְיֶה לְךָ אַרְבָּעִים יוֹם רְצוּפִים הִתְבּוֹדְדוּת, בְּוַדַּאי יִהְיֶה לְךָ שִׁנּוּי לְטוֹבָה. פַּעַם אַחַת אָמַר לְר' שְׁמוּאֵל מִטֶּעפְּלִיק עֶר מֵיינְט עֶר אִיז שׁוֹין פַארְטִיג, פַארְגֶעס נִיט אַז דִּי מִשְׁנָה זָאגְט (הוּא חוֹשֵׁב שֶׁהוּא כְּבָר מְסֻדָּר, אַל תִּשְׁכַּח שֶׁהַמִּשְׁנָה אוֹמֶרֶת) כָּל שֶׁעִסְקוֹ עִם הַנָּשִׁים סוּרוֹ רַע. וְר' אֶפְרַיִם חֲתָנוֹ שָׁמַע זֹאת, וְנִכְנַס בְּלִבּוֹ מְאֹד לִלְמֹד קַל וָחֹמֶר בְּעַצְמוֹ, שֶׁחָמִיו הָר' שְׁמוּאֵל הַנַּ"ל הוּא זָקֵן, וְהוּא הָיָה רַךְ בְּשָׁנִים כַּמָּה הוּא צָרִיךְ לִירֹא מִזֶּה, כִּי הוּא גַּם־כֵּן הָיָה עִסְקוֹ בְּתַכְשִׁיטֵי נָשִׁים. וּפַעַם אַחַת מָצְאוּ לְר' אֶפְרַיִם בֶּן ר' נַפְתָּלִי הַנַּ"ל בְּעִיר קִיֶעב עַל הַיָּרִיד, כִּי מִסְחָרוֹ הָיָה עִם מַרְגָּלִיּוֹת וְעָסַק בְּהִתְבּוֹדְדוּת. כִּי הָיָה אָז בְּלִבּוֹ הִרְהוּר תְּשׁוּבָה בַּמֶּה הוּא עוֹסֵק עַתָּה, וְכִי זֶה הוּא הַתַּכְלִית, וְכִי בִּשְׁבִיל זֶה בָּא לָעוֹלָם וְהָיָה עוֹמֵד בַּצַּד וּבוֹכֶה. וְשָׁאַל אוֹתוֹ אֶחָד מֵאַנְשֵׁי שְׁלוֹמֵנוּ מִפְּנֵי מָה בּוֹכֶה וְהֵשִׁיב לוֹ. אָמַר לוֹ וְכִי פֹּה הַמָּקוֹם לִבְכּוֹת, הוֹלְכִין לְבֵית הַמִּדְרָשׁ וְשָׁם תִּבְכֶּה. וְעָנָה לוֹ רַבִּי אֶפְרַיִם הַנַּ"ל שֶׁרַבֵּנוּ הַקָּדוֹשׁ אָמַר שֶׁבְּמָקוֹם שֶׁמַּגִּיעַ לְאָדָם הִרְהוּרֵי תְּשׁוּבָה, צָרִיךְ בְּאוֹתוֹ הַמָּקוֹם אֲפִלּוּ בְּאֶמְצַע הַשּׁוּק לְהִתְבּוֹדֵד וּלְדַבֵּר דִּבּוּרִים לִפְנֵי הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ, כִּי עַד שֶׁיֵּלֵךְ לְבֵית הַמִּדְרָשׁ יֵלְכוּ מִמֶּנּוּ הִרְהוּרֵי תְּשׁוּבָה:
segments.en: § 53 — A Letter from R. Yitzchak: Cannot Open His Mouth in Hisbodedus; Moharan"as: So Too Dovid HaMelekh — He Sat Himself Down and Sighed — Until Hashem Helped; R. Moshe Breslover and R. Pinchas Yehoshua on Their Preferred Times for Moharan"as's Words Once a letter came to Moharan"as from his son R. Yitzchak z"l — apologizing to him that when he goes to do hisbodedus he cannot open his mouth — and because of this it is very difficult for him to do hisbodedus. And Moharan"as z"l answered him: this happened also with Dovid HaMelekh, peace be upon him — when he went to do hisbodedus his mouth was closed — and he could not do hisbodedus and express his heart before Hashem, may He be blessed. But Dovid HaMelekh, peace be upon him, was very wise in the service of Hashem, may He be blessed — and he did not leave from there — and sat himself down there — and sighed greatly from the depth of his heart — and cried out to Hashem, may He be blessed, about this — that his heart and his mouth were closed. Until Hashem, may He be blessed, had mercy on him and helped him — and he opened his mouth and spoke with very great arousal to Hashem, may He be blessed. And this is hinted in the verse [II Samuel 7]: "And Dovid sat before Hashem" — that is what is written there "before Hashem" — namely at the time he went to do hisbodedus — in that very place he sat himself. R. Moshe Breslover said: the words of Moharan"as after Havdalah are better for him. And R. Pinchas Yehoshua was accustomed to say that the words of the third Shabbos meal are better for him.

segments.he:
מד
מוֹהֲרַנַ"ת זַ"ל כְּשֶׁהָיָה בְּלֶעמְבֶּערְג נִכְנַס לְהַפְּרוֹפֶסוֹר הַזֶּה שֶׁרַבֵּנוּ הַקָּדוֹשׁ הָיָה אֶצְלוֹ, וְהָיָה רוֹצֶה לִשְׁמֹעַ אֵיזֶה דִּבּוּר מֵרַבֵּנוּ הַקָּדוֹשׁ שֶׁהָיָה מְדַבֵּר שָׁמָּה. וְעָנָה לוֹ שֶׁהוּא אֵינוֹ זוֹכֵר, מֵהַטִּרְדָּה שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ כָּל הַיּוֹם. מִזֶּה יְכוֹלִין לִלְמוֹד אֵיךְ צְרִיכִין לַחֲזֹר לִשְׁמֹעַ דִּבּוּר מֵרַבֵּנוּ הַקָּדוֹשׁ:
segments.en: § 54 — R. Nossan Leybli Reuven's Entered Moharan"as's Home Daily; Moharan"as Did Not Speak Fear of Heaven Every Day — But If He Spoke Once: "I Have Already Received It Forever" R. Nossan Leybli Reuven's entered Moharan"as z"l's home every day. And he recounted that Moharan"as did not speak words of fear of heaven every day — but if he had spoken once words of fear of heaven: Hob ikh shoyn op ginumen far shtendik! [I have already received it forever!]

segments.he:
מה
פַּעַם אַחַת אָמַר מוֹהֲרַנַ"ת זַ"ל, אַצַדִּיק אַז עֶר שְׁטַארְבְּט אַצַדִּיק, דָּאס אִיז דְּבַר פֶּלֶא (צַדִּיק שֶׁהוּא נִפְטַר כְּצַדִּיק, זֶה הוּא דְבַר פֶּלֶא). פַּעַם אַחַת אָמַר אַ וִיא אַוַויְסֶע בָּארְד אוּן נָאךְ אַבְּרֶסְלֶבֶר חָסִיד (זָקָן לָבָן וְעוֹד חֲסִיד בְּרֶסְלֶב). וּפַעַם אַחַת בָּא מוֹהֲרַנַ"ת זַ"ל לַמִּשְׁנָה שֶׁל עֲקַבְיָא בֶּן מַהֲלַלְאֵל אוֹמֵר הִסְתַּכֵּל וְכוּ' וְנִתְלַהֵב מְאֹד מְאֹד, וְאָמַר בְּזֶה הַלָּשׁוֹן, פַאר וָואס אִיז רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בַּר יוֹחָאי גִיוֶוען רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בַּר יוֹחָאי, וַויְל עֶר הָאט דָּאס גִּיוִויסְט. פַאר וָואס אִיז גִּיוֶוען דֶּער הָאֲרִ"י הַקָּדוֹשׁ דֶּער הָאֲרִ"י הַקָּדוֹשׁ, וַוייל עֶר הָאט גֶּעוִויסְט. פַאר וָואס אִיז גִּיוֶוען דֶּער בַּעַל שֵׁם טוֹב הַקָּדוֹשׁ דֶּער בַּעַל שֵׁם טוֹב הַקָּדוֹשׁ, וַויְל עֶר הָאט גֶּעוִויסְט. פַאר וָואס אִיז גִּיוֶוען דֶּער הֵיילִיקֶער רַבִּי דֶּער הֵיילִיקֶער רַבִּי, וַויְל עֶר הָאט גִּיוִויסְט. פַאר וָואס בִּין אִיךְ אוֹיְךְ אִיךְ, וַוייל אִיךְ וֵוייס (מַדּוּעַ הָרַשְׁבִּ"י הָיָה רַשְׁבִּ"י כֵּיוָן שֶׁיָּדַע זֹאת, וּמַדּוּעַ הַאֲרִ"י הַקָּדוֹשׁ הָיָה הָאֲרִ"י הַקָּדוֹשׁ כֵּיוָן שֶׁיָּדַע זֹאת, וּמַדּוּעַ הַבַּעַשֵׁ"ט הָיָה הַבַּעַשֵׁ"ט כֵּיוָן שֶׁיָּדַע זֹאת, וּמַדּוּעַ רַבֵּנוּ הַקָּדוֹשׁ הָיָה רַבֵּנוּ הַקָּדוֹשׁ כֵּיוָן שֶׁיָּדַע זֹאת, וּמַדּוּעַ אֲנִי כְּמוֹ שֶׁאֲנִי כֵּיוָן שֶׁאֲנִי יוֹדֵעַ), וּפַעַם אַחַת אָמַר מוֹהֲרַנַ"ת זַ"ל הֲגַם הַחֵן הָאֱמֶת שֶׁהָיָה עַל הַבַּעַל שֵׁם טוֹב הַקָּדוֹשׁ וְעַל רַבֵּנוּ הַקָּדוֹשׁ, זֶה הַחֵן לֹא נִמְצָא בִּי, אֲבָל מֵחֵן שֶׁל שֶׁקֶר אֲנִי נָקִי. אוּן אִיבֶּער דֶּעם הִתְנוֹצְצוּת אֱלֹקוּת וָואס אִיז דָּא אִין מִיר אִיבֶּער דֶּעם אִיז מַיין דַּאוֶונֶען אַנְדֶערְשׁ, אוּן מַיין לֶערְנִין אַנְדֶערְשׁ, אוּן מַיין עֶסִין אַנְדֶערְשׁ, אוּן מַיין רֶעדִין מִיט מֶענְטְשִׁין אִיז אַנְדֶערְשׁ (וּבִגְלַל הַהִתְנוֹצְצוּת אֱלֹקוּת שֶׁיֵּשׁ בִּי, לָכֵן תְּפִילָתִי אַחֶרֶת,
לִמּוּדִי אַחֶרֶת, אַכִילָתִי אַחֶרֶת, וְדִבּוּרִי עִם בְּנֵי אָדָם אַחֶרֶת):
segments.en:
§ 55 — "Abomination of Hashem Is Every Proud Heart" — He Stressed the Word "Every" — Even in Torah and Prayer Once Moharan"as said: "An abomination of Hashem is every proud heart" [to'avas Hashem kol gevah lev — Proverbs 16:5]. And he stressed the word kol [every] — even in Torah and prayer.

§ 56 — At the Time of the Machloikes: "All This Is Because You Are Not Proper Jews"; They: "At Least We Want to Hold Onto Rebbe"; Moharan"as: "You Are as You Are — and You Want to Hold Onto Such a Rebbe — Therefore What Passes Over You Passes" At the time of the machloikes [opposition] Moharan"as said to the men of our fellowship: all this is because you are not proper Jews as you should be. They said to him: at least we want to hold onto our master z"l. Moharan"as z"l said to them: Ir zent vi azoy ir zent — un ir vilt zikh nokh halṭn in azoy a Rebn — iber dem geyt oyf aykh azoynes iber! [You are as you are — and you still want to hold onto such a Rebbe — therefore what passes over you passes!]

segments.he:
מו
פַּעַם אַחַת סִפְּרוּ לִפְנֵי מוֹהֲרַנַ"ת זַ"ל, מַה שֶׁנּוֹהֲגִים הַחֲסִידִים שֶׁמַּנִּיחִים מַשְׁקֶה הַמְשַׁכֵּר תַּחַת הַכַּר שֶׁלָּהֶם, וּבִזְמַן שֶׁהֵם מְקִיצִים מִשְּׁנָתָם שׁוֹאֲלִים מָשִׁיחַ עֲדַיִן לֹא בָּא, שׁוֹתִין מַשְׁקֶה הַמְשַׁכֵּר הַזֶּה וּמִשְׁתַּכְּרִים וְחוֹזְרִים לִשְׁנָתָם. כִּי הֵם אוֹמְרִים שֶׁכָּל זְמַן שֶׁמָּשִׁיחַ לֹא בָּא, צָרִיךְ לְיַשֵּׁן הַיֵּצֶר הָרָע. מֶען דַּארְף פַאר שְׁלָאפִין דֶּעם יֵצֶר הָרָע, כִּי בִּזְמַן הַשֵּׁנָה אִי אֶפְשָׁר לַחֲטֹא. וְאָמַר לָהֶם מוֹהֲרַנַ"ת זַ"ל שֶׁזֶּה אֵין עֵצָה, אֶלָּא צְרִיכִים לְהַנִּיחַ תְּהִלִּים מְרַאֲשׁוֹתָיו וּבִזְמַן שֶׁמֵּקִיץ מֵהַשֵּׁנָה אִם מָשִׁיחַ לֹא בָּא צְרִיכִין מֵחָדָשׁ (לִצְעֹק מִמַּעֲמַקִּים מֵעֹמֶק הַלֵּב)
לוֹמַר תְּהִלִּים:
segments.en: § 57 — When Orphaned After His Mother He Asked Rebbe How to Do Good for Her; Rebbe: "Say Asher Yatsar Seriously" — Aimed at His Thought That One Must Say Asher Yatsar At the time when Moharan"as was orphaned after his mother — he asked our master z"l how he could do good for his mother. And he answered him: Du zolst makhn Asher Yatsar ernst! [You shall say Asher Yatsar with seriousness!] And he aimed at his thought — that one must truly say the blessing of Asher Yatsar.

segments.he:
מז־מח
ר' מֵאִיר מִטֶּעפְּלִיק הָיָה מִגְּדוֹלֵי מְקֹרָבֵי מוֹהֲרַנַ"ת זַ"ל. וְהָיָה דַּרְכּוֹ לִקְבֹּל לִפְנֵי מוֹהֲרַנַ"ת זַ"ל שֶׁהָעֲבוֹדָה אֵינוֹ מִתְנַהֵג אֶצְלוֹ כַּסֵּדֶר וְהוּא הָיָה מְחַזֵּק אוֹתוֹ. פַּעַם אַחַת בָּא לְפָנָיו וְאָמַר לוֹ שֶׁזֶּה אֵיזֶה זְמַן שֶׁהָעֲבוֹדָה מִתְנַהֵג אֶצְלוֹ כַּסֵּדֶר. אָמַר לוֹ מוֹהֲרַנַ"ת בְּזֶה הַלָּשׁוֹן: אִיךְ וֵוייס נִיט אֶפְשָׁר אִיז דִּיר גּוּט, אוּן אִיךְ וֵוייס אַז כָּל זְמַן מָשִׁיחַ אִיז נָאךְ נִיט גֶּעקוּמֶען, דַּארְף מֶען הַאלְטֶען אִין אֵיין רַיְיסֶען (אֲנִי לֹא יוֹדֵעַ אוּלַי לְךָ טוֹב, אֲבָל אֲנִי יוֹדֵעַ שֶׁכָּל זְמַן שֶׁמָּשִׁיחַ עוֹד לֹא בָּא צָרִיךְ לֶאֱחוֹז כָּל הַזְּמַן בְּלַעֲמוֹל וְלַעֲמוֹל). אָמַר מוֹהֲרַנַ"ת זַ"ל מִפְּנֵי מָה זָכִיתִי שֶׁלְּעֵת זִקְנָתִי הוֹלֵךְ לִי הָעֲבוֹדָה כַּסֵּדֶר, מִפְּנֵי שֶׁהָיָה לִי בִּימֵי נְעוּרַי הִתְבּוֹדְדוּת הַרְבֵּה. מוֹהֲרַנַ"ת זַ"ל הָיָה לוֹ בְּרָכָה מֵרַבֵּנוּ זַ"ל אֲשֶׁר בְּעֵת שֶׁמַּנִּיחַ אֶת עַצְמוֹ לִישֹׁן יִישַׁן תֵּכֶף. פַּעַם אַחַת סִפְּרוּ לִפְנֵי מוֹהֲרַנַ"ת עַל מְפֻרְסָם אֶחָד שֶׁמִּתְפַּלֵּל בַּחֲשַׁאי, וְנִתְרַגֵּשׁ מוֹהֲרַנַ"ת וְאָמַר הֵם מְדַמִּין אֶת עַצְמָם לְרַבֵּנוּ הַקָּדוֹשׁ, נִתְקַיֵּם אֶצְלוֹ שֶׁמֶן בַּחֲשַׁאי כַּמְבֹאָר בְּהַתּוֹרָה כ"א. וְאָמַר בְּזֶה הַלָּשׁוֹן זָאלִין זֵיי זִיךְ אַזוֹי מוּטְשִׁין אוּן דַּאוֶונֶען אַזוֹי וִוי אִיךְ מוּטְשִׁי זִיךְ (שֶׁהֵם יִתְיַגְעוּ בַּתְּפִלָּה כְּמוֹ שֶׁאֲנִי מִתְיַגֵּעַ). פַּעַם אַחַת אָמַר מוֹהֲרַנַ"ת זַ"ל לִפְנֵי אַנְשֵׁי שְׁלוֹמֵנוּ אֶת הַתּוֹרָה (ט"ו) שֶׁל אוֹר הַגָּנוּז הַמַּתְחִיל בְּזֶה הַלָּשׁוֹן, מִי שֶׁרוֹצֶה לִטְעֹם טַעַם אוֹר הַגָּנוּז וְכוּ' צָרִיךְ לַעֲסֹק בִּבְחִינַת מִשְׁפָּט שֶׁהוּא הִתְבּוֹדְדוּת. וּכְשֶׁסִּיֵּם הַתּוֹרָה וְהָלְכוּ קְצָת אֲנָשִׁים וְנִשְׁאֲרוּ רַק אַנְשֵׁי שְׁלוֹמֵנוּ. עָנָה וְאָמַר לָהֶם שֶׁהַפֵּרוּשׁ שֶׁל הַתּוֹרָה הוּא כָּךְ מִי שֶׁרוֹצֶה לִטְעֹם אוֹר רַבֵּנוּ הַקָּדוֹשׁ שֶׁהוּא
אוֹר הַגָּנוּז יַרְבֶּה בְּהִתְבּוֹדְדוּת:
segments.en: § 58 — R. Nachman Tulshiner Came to Moharan"as's Attic and Saw Him Writing; Did Not Want to Disturb; Afterwards Saw the Written Prayer "Lamah Panekha Tastir" — Full of Tears Once R. Nachman Tulshiner came to Moharan"as's attic — and saw that he was writing — and did not want to disturb him. And afterwards he saw the writing of the prayer "Why do You hide Your face" [lamah panekha tastir] — which was full of tears.

segments.he:
מט
זוּגָתוֹ שֶׁל מוֹהֲרַנַ"ת הָלְכָה לְעוֹלָמָהּ בִּזְמַן שֶׁהָיָה לְקִיחַת הַנֶּעקְרִיטִין (גִיּוּס צְעִירִים יְהוּדִים לִצְבָא הַצָאר הָרוּסִי) וּמֵתָה מֵחֲמַת הַצַּעַר הַנַּ"ל. וְאָמַר עַל זֶה מוֹהֲרַנַ"ת שֶׁצְּרִיכִין לִבְכּוֹת עַל זֶה כְּמוֹ עַל הַגְּזֵרָה הַנַּ"ל. ר' יִצְחָק בְּנוֹ שֶׁל מוֹהֲרַנַ"ת זַ"ל הָיָה אָבִיו מַשִּׂיאוֹ לִטְשֶׁרְקַאז וּלְאַחַר הַחֲתֻנָּה הָיְתָה זוּגָתוֹ מְמָאֵן אוֹתוֹ, וְחוֹתְנוֹ אוֹהֲבוֹ מְאֹד וְלֹא רָצָה לְהַנִּיחוֹ. וְחָשַׁב בְּדַעְתּוֹ שֶׁעַכְשָׁו הִיא קְטַנָּה וְאֵין לָהּ שֵׂכֶל שָׁלֵם, וּמֵחֲמַת זֶה מְמָאֶנֶת בּוֹ, וְאִם יִשְׁהֶה שָׁנָה אוֹ יוֹתֵר יִהְיֶה לָהּ דַּעַת יוֹתֵר אֶפְשָׁר שֶׁתִּרְצֶה. וּבָא מוֹהֲרַנַ"ת זַ"ל וְאָמַר לִמְחֻתָּנוֹ הַנַּ"ל שֶׁיִּבְחֹר לוֹ מַה שֶּׁיִּרְצֶה, אוֹ שֶׁיָּדוּר עִמָּהּ וְאִם לָאו יִהְיֶה גֵּט. וְהוּא עָנָה לוֹ כַּנַּ"ל שֶׁיַּמְתִּין אֵיזֶה שָׁנִים עַד שֶׁתִּתְגַּדֵּל וְיִהְיֶה לָהּ שֵׂכֶל יוֹתֵר, כִּי גֵּט לֹא רָצָה חוֹתְנוֹ כִּי אָהַב אוֹתוֹ מְאֹד, וְלָדוּר עִמּוֹ הִיא לֹא רָצְתָה. וּכְשֶׁרָאָה מוֹהֲרַנַ"ת זַ"ל שֶׁאֵין לוֹ שׁוּם עֵצָה, וַיֵּצֵא לַחוּץ וְאָחַז בְּשַׂעֲרוֹת רֹאשׁוֹ וְצָעַק בְּקוֹל גָּדוֹל גִּיוַואלְד עֶר קוֹיְלִיט מַיְין קִינְד (אֲהָהּ! הוּא רוֹצֵחַ אֶת בְּנִי). עַד שֶׁנִּתְאַסְּפוּ כַּמָּה אֲנָשִׁים וְהִכְנִיסוּ עַצְמָם שֶׁיִּהְיֶה גֵּט. וּפַעַם אַחַת הָיָה מַעֲשֶׂה, שֶׁר' נָתָן הָיָה לוֹ אָח וּשְׁמוֹ לֵיְיבּוּשׁ. וְהָיָה לוֹ מְעַט זְמַן קְטָטָה עִם זוּגָתוֹ וּפֵרַשׁ מִמֶּנָּה. וְאַחַר־כָּךְ חָזְרָה וְנִתְפַּתֵּית וְנִתְרַצָּה וְנַעֲשָׂה שָׁלוֹם עִמָּהּ. וְאָמַר אָז מוֹהֲרַנַ"ת זַ"ל שֶׁזֶּה שֶׁחָזַר וְנַעֲשָׂה שָׁלוֹם עִמָּהּ, זֶה נַעֲשֵׂית בְּכֹחַ הַצַּדִּיק הָאֱמֶת שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ כֹּחַ לַהֲפֹךְ מִשְּׁמַד לְרָצוֹן. וּפַעַם אַחַת בִּימֵי מוֹהֲרַנַ"ת זַ"ל הָיָה אֶחָד שֶׁנָּשָׂא אִשָּׁה רָעָה אֲפִלּוּ לַאֲחֵרִים וּלְאַחַר הַנִּשּׂוּאִין נוֹדַע לוֹ וְלֹא יָדַע מַה לַּעֲשׂוֹת כִּי הִקְנִיטָה אוֹתוֹ מְאֹד, וְשָׁאַל לְמוֹהֲרַנַ"ת זַ"ל עֵצָה מַה לַּעֲשׂוֹת, וְהֵשִׁיב לוֹ עֵצָה שֶׁיִּתְפַּלֵּל חֲצִי שָׁנָה שְׁלֵמָה עַל זֶה בְּכָל יוֹם שָׁעָה
מְיֻחָד דְּהַיְנוּ שֶׁתִּהְיֶה לְהַלָּן טוֹב אֵלָיו וְלֹא כָּל־כָּךְ רַע וְכוּ':
segments.en: § 59 — A Man of Our Fellowship Was a Merchant Traveling With Goods; Rain Fell; He Spread a Canopy and Sat to Learn; Moharan"as Passed and Called Him; Afterwards Said: The Man Was Very Happy About the Rain — Because Through It He Could Serve Hashem One of the men of our fellowship was a merchant traveling with goods — and on the road rain fell. And the man spread a canopy [palatke] — a tent — and sat to study. And in the meantime Moharan"as z"l passed and called him. Afterwards Moharan"as recounted: he saw that the man was very happy about the rain — because through this he could serve Hashem, may He be blessed — for certainly now it was impossible to trade.

segments.he:
נ
פַּעַם אַחַת אָמַר מוֹהֲרַנַ"ת, אֵיךְ אֶפְשָׁר שֶׁיִּהְיֶה עוֹלָם הַזֶּה
כְּשֶׁיֵּשׁ תַּאֲוָה הַיְדוּעָה בָּעוֹלָם:
segments.en: § 60 — "The War of Gog and Magog Is Not Mentioned in the Megilas Setarim — Meaning There Will Be Heresy in the World — and This Will Be the Test for Us and for Mashiach" Moharan"as would say: the war of Gog and Magog is not mentioned in the Megilas Setarim — this implies there will be heresy [apikorsus] in the world — and this will be the test for us and for Mashiach.

segments.he:
נא
פַּעַם אַחַת אָמַר אֶחָד לְמוֹהֲרַנַ"ת אוֹמְרִים עֲלֵיכֶם שֶׁאַתֶּם אוֹמְרִים מֶ'וֶועט שְׁמַיְיסִין עַל שֶׁלֹּא הָיָה (שֶׁיַּעֲנִישׁוּ בִּגְלַל שֶׁלֹּא הָיָה) בְּרֶסְלֶבֶר חָסִיד. וַיֹּאמֶר אֵלָיו אֵינִי אוֹמֵר כֵּן, אֶלָּא שֶׁיִּלְקוּ עַל הַפְּגָמִים, אִם תִּרְאֶה פְּגָמֶיךָ הַגְּדוֹלִים וְתָבִין, אִם הָיִיתָ
בְּרֶסְלֶבֶר חָסִיד לֹא הָיָה לְךָ הַפְּגָמִים הָאֵלֶּה:
segments.en:
§ 61 — A Rav Sent That R. Nesanel Teplik Should Not Let Moharan"as Lodge; R. Nesanel Refused; The Rav Cursed the Daughter; Moharan"as: "Now the Rav Has Opened My Mouth to Pray for Her" — She Had a Son; R. Nesanel's Generosity; His Illness; Moharan"as: "I Want Him to Make the Effort Himself"; The Rav Moved: "Surely You Should Wear Silk"; Moharan"as: "That Too Is R. Nesanel's Obligation" Once a certain Rav sent to R. Nesanel of Teplik that he should not let Moharan"as lodge at his home when he came to Teplik. And he answered him: "This is impossible — for Moharan"as has no place to lodge except at mine — and what the Rav frightens me with — what can I do?" And so it was. And R. Nesanel feared lest Moharan"as hear of the aforementioned letter — and therefore sent a letter to Moharan"as z"l that he was not at all listening to the words of the aforementioned Rav. And afterwards when Moharan"as came to Teplik — he lodged in the home of Rabbi Nesanel with great honor — and he made a great meal for him — and his daughter quickly made fried dough [tayglikh] in honor of Moharan"as. Afterwards Moharan"as saw that R. Nesanel had a little pride. He said to him: Efsher meynstu az on dir volt ikh keyn stantsye nit gihat — ikh on dir kan zikh bageyn — du on mir nit! [Perhaps you think that without you I would have had no lodging — I without you can manage — you without me cannot!] Afterwards the aforementioned Rav heard this matter — and said that because of this matter R. Nesanel's daughter will have no children. And she said: what can I do? Afterwards Moharan"as said to R. Nesanel: "Now the Rav has opened my mouth to pray for her to Hashem, may He be blessed." And she was blessed with a male child. And R. Nesanel was close to our master z"l — and once gave our master z"l ten gold coins [adumim]. And our master z"l praised him and said he has never had such. And he said: he loves the coins of R. Nesanel — because he was a great miser — and for him it was mesiras nefesh [self-sacrifice] to overcome his nature. Once he promised to give Moharan"as twelve silver rubles for the building of the kloyz [study hall] — and gave him first three silver rubles — and afterwards gave him again three silver rubles — until he gave it all in several installments. And when R. Nesanel was ill — R. Nathan came to him. R. Nesanel said to R. Nathan: "Fulfill with me the Gemara — 'he extended his hand to him' etc." [granting recovery]. Moharan"as said to him: not every person can do this thing. R. Nesanel said: I believe you can do this thing. Moharan"as said to him: not for every person can one do this thing. Afterwards Moharan"as left him — and went through the kitchen. And he said to the daughter of R. Nesanel: if R. Nesanel gives charity beyond his capacity — perhaps he will still live. She said to him: I will go and tell this to my father. Moharan"as said to her: Ikh vil er zol zikh aleyn onshtosn! [I want him to push himself on his own!] And once Moharan"as was together with the aforementioned Rav — and the Rav spoke of R. Nesanel's miserliness — and recounted then that a certain posek's ruling was not accepted because he was a miser. And R. Nathan nodded his head as if he knew. And the Rav bowed his head to Moharan"as that he should name him. And Moharan"as told him. And the Rav was greatly moved and said to Moharan"as: "Surely you should wear silk garments!" And Moharan"as answered him: Dos oykh iz R. Nesanel'sn khiyuv! [That too is R. Nesanel's obligation!]

§ 62 — Torah §1 Found in a Different Version After First Printing; Preferred the Later Version; Therefore Printed Torah §1 With the Story Tales; The Maggid of Tirhavitze Was Moved: "They Are Higher Than Zohar — Higher Than Tikkunim"; Who Is Greater — the Small One Close to a Tzadik or the Great One Not Close? — The Mishkan and Moshe Torah §1 — Moharan"as found it after the first printing in a different style — not as it was printed in the first printing — and what he found afterwards seemed better to him. And therefore when he printed the Story Tales — he printed Torah §1 alongside the Story Tales. And afterwards he printed it in Lemberg as it is printed now. A certain Rav was jealous of our master z"l — because the Maggid of Tirhavitze was traveling to him — and he was accustomed to send people to the Maggid and they spoke slander against our master z"l etc. And the Maggid went to his father-in-law R. Yitzchak — who was close to our master z"l — and asked him if he had writings from our master z"l. And he showed him Torah §2 — Emor el hakohanim. And the Maggid was greatly moved and said: "What shall I say about this Torah — it is Zohar — they are higher than Zohar. They are Tikkunim — they are higher than Tikkunim." And he greatly disparaged the aforementioned slanderers. One asked Moharan"as: who is greater — the small one who is close to a Tzadik — or the great one who is not close? He said to him: was it not in the days of Moshe our teacher, peace be upon him — that if one did a great thing for the Mishkan and did not bring it to Moshe our teacher — it certainly had no importance at all? But whoever did a small thing and brought it to Moshe — it was certainly very valued. And he then said the aforementioned Torah §2 — that specifically Moshe alone can raise level upon level each one to its place.

segments.he:
נב
הִלְכוֹת מַתָּנָה הֲלָכָה ד' "וַיֵּצֵא יַעֲקֹב" נֶאֶמְרָה בְּשַׁבָּת בַּבֹּקֶר אַחַר שֶׁנָּטַל יָדָיו לֶאֱכֹל שַׁחֲרִית, הִתְחִיל לוֹמַר עַד שֶׁכִּמְעַט
נַעֲשָׂה עֶרֶב, וְכִמְעַט שֶׁלֹּא אָכְלוּ סְעֻדָּה שְׁלִישִׁית:
segments.en: § 63 — Told That R. Naftali Is an Angry Person; Moharan"as: "I Did Not Know He Is So Great — That Despite All This He Is R. Naftali — the Adversary Cannot Fell Him Through Anger"; The Three Decrees — Tach, Ganti, Nekritin; Rebbe Said: "I Uncovered His Face and Saw It Was My Naftali"; During Nekritin — R. Naftali Was in Stripping of Materiality and Did Not Hear the Tumult of the Whole City Once they told Moharan"as: R. Naftali is an angry person. And Moharan"as said: "I did not know he is so great — that despite all this he is R. Naftali — that the adversary cannot fell him through anger." And once some people were gossiping with each other — and one asked the other: why did Hashem, may He be blessed, make the decree of the nekritin here in Russia? — for the decree of Tach [1648] was understandable — as punishment for opposing the holy Arizal. And the other answered: perhaps because they tore the books of R. Nachman of Breslov. And R. Naftali recounted from this and said: because the world opposed the holy Arizal — the decree of Tach was decreed on the world. And because they opposed the Baal Shem Tov z"l — the decree of Ganti was decreed on the world [which was after the passing of the Baal Shem Tov in the year 5520]. And because there was opposition against our master z"l — the decree of the nekritin was decreed on the world — and all the decrees until the coming of our righteous Mashiach — speedily in our days, Amen. And once our master z"l recounted: I saw in the upper world that one was praying some prayer etc. [and greatly praised the prayer] — Hob ikh oyfgidekṭ dos ponim — hob ikh gizen — az dos iz mayn Naftali! [I uncovered the face — and I saw — that this is my Naftali!] And once there was a matter during the nekritin — for the way was that even one who had a release document [bilet] — they would search and take the bilet and tear it and make a false accusation that he has no bilet — in order to take him as a soldier. And there was one who hired his son to be at R. Naftali's. And once they came to Rabbi Naftali's and found the young man — and asked for the bilet. And the father feared they would tear the bilet — and therefore made a noise until the whole city gathered — and then he was no longer afraid to show the bilet — for all would be witnesses. And Rabbi Naftali was then praying mincha — and the father feared Rabbi Naftali would be upset that he had disturbed his prayer. And at the time of the meal he asked him to forgive him. And Rabbi Naftali answered him: he knows nothing at all of the whole matter — for his prayer was in the stripping of materiality [hitpashtus hagashmiyus] — until the tumult of the whole city that was in his home — he did not hear at all.

segments.he:
נג
פַּעַם אַחַת בָּא מִכְתָּב לְמוֹהֲרַנַ"ת מִבְּנוֹ הָר' יִצְחָק זַ"ל וְהִתְנַצֵּל לְפָנָיו כִּי בְּעֵת שֶׁהוֹלֵךְ לְהִתְבּוֹדֵד אֵינוֹ יָכוֹל לִפְתֹּחַ אֶת פִּיו, וּמִפְּנֵי זֶה קָשֶׁה לוֹ מְאֹד לְהִתְבּוֹדֵד. וְהֵשִׁיב לוֹ מוֹהֲרַנַ"ת זַ"ל שֶׁזֶּה הָיָה גַּם־כֵּן אֵצֶל דָּוִד הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם שֶׁבְּעֵת שֶׁהָלַךְ לְהִתְבּוֹדֵד נִסְתַּם פִּיו, וְלֹא הָיָה יָכוֹל לְהִתְבּוֹדֵד וּלְפָרֵשׁ אֶת לִבּוֹ לִפְנֵי הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ, אֲבָל דָּוִד הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם הָיָה חָכָם מְאֹד בַּעֲבוֹדַת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ, וְלֹא הָלַךְ מִשָּׁם וְיִשֵּׁב אֶת עַצְמוֹ שָׁם וַיִּתְאַנַּח מְאֹד מֵעֹמֶק הַלֵּב, וְצָעַק לְהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ עַל זֶה מַה שֶּׁלִּבּוֹ וּפִיו סָתוּם. עַד שֶׁרִחֵם עָלָיו הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ וַעֲזָרוֹ שֶׁפָּתַח אֶת פִּיו וְדִבֵּר בְּהִתְעוֹרְרוּת גָּדוֹל מְאֹד לְהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ. וְזֶה מְרֻמָּז בְּפָסוּק (שְׁמוּאֵל־ב ז) שֶׁכָּתוּב שָׁם וַיֵּשֶׁב דָּוִד לִפְנֵי ה', הַיְנוּ מַה שֶּׁכָּתוּב לִפְנֵי ה', דְּהַיְנוּ בְּעֵת
שֶׁהָלַךְ לְהִתְבּוֹדֵד, בְּזֶה הַמָּקוֹם יִשֵּׁב אֶת עַצְמוֹ:
ר' מֹשֶׁה בְּרֶסְלֶבֶר אָמַר שֶׁיּוֹתֵר טוֹב לוֹ הַדִּבּוּרִים שֶׁל מוֹהֲרַנַ"ת שֶׁל אַחַר הַבְדָּלָה. וְר' פִּינְחָס יְהוֹשֻׁעַ הָיָה אוֹמֵר
שֶׁיּוֹתֵר טוֹב לוֹ הַדִּבּוּרִים שֶׁל שָׁלֹשׁ סְעֻדּוֹת:
segments.en: § 64 — At the Time of Moharan"as's Distress — Last Market Before Pesach and No Pesach Needs; Wife Taught Him "a Chapter of Melancholy"; After Prayer His Face Was Yellow and Joyful — His Bitachon Was So Strong; R. Yosil Hoizner of Tulchin; The Opponents Tried to Take Away R. Yitzchak's Post; Moharan"as: "The Journey to Uman for Rosh HaShanah Supersedes Everything — with Mesiras Nefesh"; Erev Yom Kippur — Wife Made Peace; Moharan"as: "A Success That Yom Kippur Always Falls Right After Rosh HaShanah" Once at a time of distress for Moharan"as — the last market before Erev Pesach had arrived — and he still had no Pesach needs. And therefore in the morning of that day — still before the prayer — his wife Dishl, peace be upon her, began to complain before him — laying out her arguments that were heard by him and grieved his soul so much — that about this he testified and said afterwards before the men of our fellowship: Oy — hot zi mit mir opgilernt a perek fun marah shekhorah! [Oy — she taught me a chapter of melancholy!] Even so, when the time of prayer arrived — he strengthened himself with every kind of strengthening with all his power in faith and trust to cleave to Hashem, may He be blessed — and he prayed his prayer. Until after the prayer R. Nachman Tulshiner testified of him — that he saw his face yellow and joyful — as if his lack were already filled. And also on that day there was a market day in Breslov — for the way of the people of Rorid near Breslov is to come there for the market. And two or three men of our fellowship came to him and gave him a proper sum — and his lack was entirely filled in every way. And the hour they gave him — R. Nachman mentioned testified — that he saw no change of extra joy on his face — because beforehand he was already full of strong bitachon — as if the filling of the lack were already in his pocket. And these people merited to be the agents for this great mitzvah. In Tulchin there was one — R. Yosil Hoizner — who merited to spend one Shabbos at our master z"l. And he was also somewhat educated in the Russian language — and was esteemed by ministers. And therefore he was among the notable citizens of the city — a man of opinion — and his words were heard. And through him R. Yitzchak son of Moharan"as z"l was appointed as director of the post office [past] in Tulchin. Afterwards when the opposition against the men of our fellowship intensified — and the opponents were permitted to do to the men of our fellowship whatever their heart desired — and whoever did not curse Moharan"as z"l was a sign he too was a Breslover and it was permitted to deprive him of livelihood. And therefore the opponents began to speak to the heart of the Rav R. Yosil mentioned — that he should also deprive R. Yitzchak mentioned of his livelihood — because he travels to his father in Breslov. And R. Yosil deflected them: "And because he travels to Breslov to his father — is this proof he is a Breslover? He is simply traveling to honor him." And the opponents were compelled to accept his words. However — when the time came to travel to Uman for Rosh HaShanah — then R. Yitzchak mentioned was truly in a predicament — if he traveled there it would be conclusive proof that he was a Breslover. And therefore he went in advance to his father Moharan"as z"l to ask his opinion: what to do now? He said to him: the journey to Uman for Rosh HaShanah supersedes everything — and one is obligated to fulfill this with mesiras nefesh. Naturally he paid no heed to anything — and for Rosh HaShanah he traveled to Uman. After Rosh HaShanah passed — R. Yitzchak mentioned understood that returning home was impossible for him now — for certainly now he was without livelihood. And his second wife too was from the opponents' side [of whom Moharan"as said: had he not already been divorced from his first wife — he would have commanded him to divorce her] — and now she too had a heard argument: "livelihood!" — if so he would need to be a wanderer among the men of our fellowship — and be entirely separated from worldly affairs. Only this he did not know — where should he first make his way. And therefore he came to his father z"l to pour out before him the bitterness of his heart — and in the end asked him: to which place to travel right now? Moharan"as z"tl — in the greatness of his wisdom and righteousness — understood differently — and said to him: on the contrary! Return home to Tulchin — and go straight home. And when your wife opens her mouth with her arguments and cries — you shall not answer anything — only be silent. When she disturbs you from some business you are engaged in at home — do not fear her — leave the business. Say to her boldly that you are the master of the house. If she raises her hand to strike you — you raise your stick. In short — do not fear her at all. And regarding livelihood — Hashem is mighty to save. And therefore R. Yitzchak mentioned hurried to fulfill his father's words — and returned to Tulchin and went straight home. And there everything was exactly as his father z"l had told him — the wife began to cry out and he was silent. She disturbed him from some business he engaged in — and he did his thing. "I am the master of the house." She tried to raise her hand against him — and he preceded her with the poker [katshkhere]. And naturally he dismissed the post office livelihood from his mind. The next day — in the course of his walking in the city street — he met the aforementioned R. Yosil — who had merited to spend one Shabbos at our master z"l. And on the contrary he himself began to speak with R. Yitzchak and asked him in wonder: "Why are you not coming to the post? Do not fear and do not be dismayed — return to the post and everything as before." When Erev Yom Kippur arrived — from the awe of the Day of Judgment — that was truly in former generations on all the seed of Israel from small to great — his wife also did so — and appeased her husband R. Yitzchak z"l — and all was peace with him as before. This dear son hurried to inform all of this to his father. Then Moharan"as z"l said jokingly: Eyn hatslokhoh far anshey shlomeynu — vos Yom Kippur gefalṭ tomed bald nokh Rosh HaShanah! [A great success for the men of our fellowship — that Yom Kippur always falls right after Rosh HaShanah!]

segments.he:
נד
ר' נָתָן לֵיבְּלִי רְאוּבֵן'ס הָיָה נִכְנַס בְּכָל יוֹם אֶל בֵּית מוֹהֲרַנַ"ת זַ"ל, וְסִפֵּר שֶׁמּוֹהַרְנַ"ת לֹא הָיָה מְדַבֵּר בְּכָל יוֹם דִּבּוּרֵי יִרְאָה, אֶלָּא שֶׁאִם הָיָה מְדַבֵּר פַּעַם אַחַת דִּבּוּרֵי יִרְאָה, הָאבּ אִיךְ
שׁוֹין אָפּ גִּינוּמֶען פַאר שְׁטֶענְדִיג (כְּבָר קִבַּלְתִּי לְתָמִיד):
segments.en: § 65 — Before Drawing Close to Rebbe Moharan"as Was Almost Distant from Learning — Fell into Complete Despair; Rebbe Said: "Abisel iz oykh gut"; Gradually Emerged from Despair; "Don't Stand Too Long on a Hard Question — Torah Is Poor Here and Rich Elsewhere" Moharan"as z"l recounted: before I drew close to our master z"l — I was almost distant from learning. Because my desire was to be one of the diligent scholars — and when I came to the house of study and some obstacle came up and I was not able to immediately study — I studied a little. And once some obstacle passed — when this happened once, twice, and three times — I had already despaired of that day — and the diligence would start from the next day. And so it happened to me on the next day in other ways — and likewise on the third day — until I fell into complete despair and became a complete idler. However when I drew close to our master z"l — and he said to me about this: Abisel iz oykh gut! [A little is also good!] When I afterwards came to the house of study and saw that I was not able to study much — only a little — and I remembered the words of our master z"l — abiseleh iz oykh gut — and therefore I studied a little. Afterwards I said: I will study a little more — and I studied a little more. And little by little I emerged from despair and became a diligent scholar. And this too helped me — what our master z"l added: that during study one should not stand too long on a hard question to answer and settle it in that very hour — for many times one cannot [do so] in that hour. Besides that — one wastes much time on it — and sometimes the whole study becomes disgusting. Therefore one should not stand long — only mark that in this place further thought is needed — and "Torah is poor in one place and rich in another" [Jerusalem Talmud, Rosh HaShanah]. And with broad knowledge in learning — the matter will settle itself on its own.

segments.he:
נה
פַּעַם אַחַת אָמַר מוֹהֲרַנַ"ת, "תּוֹעֲבַת ה' כָּל גְּבַהּ לֵב". וְדָחַק
תֵּבַת כָּל, אֲפִלּוּ בְּתוֹרָה וּתְפִלָּה:
segments.en:
§ 66 — After Rebbe's Passing: R. Avrahaml Petersburger Told Aharon Lipavetzky How in Rebbe's Final Days He Rode a Horse Fearlessly; Rebbe: "I Am So Weak That I Have Already Lost My Voice — and When One Loses the Voice Even the Merit of the Forefathers No Longer Helps — When You Will Be a Proper Jew You Will Understand This" After the passing of our master z"l — R. Avrahaml Petersburger recounted before his friend Aharon Lipavetzky, peace be upon him: how our master z"l in his final days — in the height of his weakness in Uman — it was his way every day to travel outside the city to breathe fresh air. And the men of our fellowship from there provided him every day with a hitched wagon for this. Once there was no hitched wagon for them — and they provided him a horse to ride. And I — being a merchant and knowledgeable in all worldly matters — I saw that he rode the horse without any fear — like a chosen and expert horseman. And I was among those who were first and eager to run after him — in order to be among the first with him. Suddenly our master z"l asked: "Who is running after me so energetically?" And I said: I. Then he said to me in this language: Ikh bin azoy shlaḥ — az ikh hob shoyn ongevarṭn dos kol — ikh hob shoyn gor keyn kol nit — un az men vert on dos kol — helft shoyn afile nit keyn zkhus avos. Az du vest zayn eyn erlikher Yid — vestu dos farshṭeyn! [I am so weak — that I have already lost my voice — I have no voice at all — and when one loses the voice — even the merit of the forefathers no longer helps. When you will be a proper Jew — you will understand this!] [And this is hinted and explained, said R. Avrohom, in the Torah "Sound the Faith" [tik'u emunah] — which was said that year of his passing. For it is known that every Torah he said was essentially about himself and his attainment at that very moment. And about R. Avrohom mentioned and his matter — it is explained in Koachvay Or, the composition of R. Avrohom.]

§ 1 — "Did You Hope for Salvation?" — This Asks Also: When You Were in Distress — Did You Hope for G-d's Salvation and Not Despair? The Rav R. Nachman Tulshiner z"l said: what is cited [in the tractate Shabbos 31a] — that they ask [a person after death] "Did you hope for salvation?" — and Rashi explained: for the general salvation [geulah] — in this is included that they ask each person explicitly: "When you were in distress" — did you hope for the salvation of Hashem — and did you not despair?

segments.he:
נו
בְּעֵת הַמַּחֲלֹקֶת אָמַר מוֹהֲרַנַ"ת לְאַנְשֵׁי שְׁלוֹמֵנוּ, כָּל זֶה מִפְּנֵי שֶׁאֵינְכֶם אֲנָשִׁים כְּשֵׁרִים כָּרָאוּי. אָמְרוּ לוֹ עַל־כָּל־פָּנִים אָנוּ רוֹצִים לֶאֱחֹז בְּרַבֵּנוּ זַ"ל. אָמַר לָהֶם מוֹהֲרַנַ"ת זַ"ל, אִיהְר זֶענְט וִוי אַזוֹי אִיהְר זֶענְט, אוּן אִיהְר וִוילְט זִיךְ נָאךְ הַאלְטִין אִין אַזוֹי אַ רֶבִּין אִיבֶּער דֶּעם גֵּייט אוֹיף אַייךְ אַזוֹיְנְס אִיבֶּער (אַתֶּם כְּמוֹ שֶׁאַתֶּם, וַעֲדַיִן אַתֶּם רוֹצִים לְהֵאָחֵז בְּרֶבֶּי כָּזֶה לָכֵן עוֹבֵר עֲלֵיכֶם
מַה שֶּׁעוֹבֵר):
segments.en: § 2 — R. Yisrael Leyb of Bohpol — At the Time of His Old Age Wanted to Move to Uman Near the Kloyz; R. Nachman Tulshiner Refused for Known Reasons; The Dispute Brought Before Rebbe's Grave; R. Yisrael Leyb Moved — and Did Not Complete the Year In the days of R. Nachman Tulshiner z"l — there was in Bohpol one of the men of our fellowship — a righteous and upright man — R. Yisrael Leyb the father of R. Asher Bohplier. And at the time of his old age — his desire was to move his residence to Uman — and there near the kloyz to build at his own expense a special house — and after his death it would be an inheritance belonging to the kloyz — and he would always engage in the service of Hashem — and at every opportunity be at the holy tziyun — for his way was sometimes to spend the whole night at the holy tziyun — and likewise by day after prayer without eating anything — he would go to the holy tziyun and spend there about four or five hours. And how good it would be for him to have his residence in Uman near the kloyz. But R. Nachman mentioned refused this for reasons known to him — and also because it is difficult for two Tzadikim to dwell in one place. And R. Yisrael Leyb maintained his view — and said his intention was truly for the sake of Heaven. And he said several times after his prostration at the holy tziyun that so it should be done [according to the tradition accepted among the men of our fellowship — a matter from the days of our master z"l — that when one is undecided about something — before hisbodedus one should fix in his mind the yes and the no equally — and after hisbodedus — whichever way his first thought falls — so should he do]. But it is very difficult to truly come to this level [for the imagination very very misleads a person to act according to his desired inclination — and in truth after hisbodedus his first thought follows the way his imaginary desire leans]. And once R. Nachman z"l recounted: we were together at the tziyun of our master z"l — and R. Yisrael Leyb mentioned said to him: let us bring our judgment before our master z"l. At the hour he said this to me — trembling and shaking seized me — for this is the aspect of "one who hands judgment to Heaven" — but what to do — and it is impossible to refuse this. I said to him: if so — let each of us set out his arguments before our master z"l — and so we did. When we came down from there — R. Yisrael Leyb mentioned was firm in his view — that his first thought was again that he should do as his heart desires. And he moved his residence to Uman near the kloyz — and did not complete his year, G-d have mercy.

segments.he:
נז
בְּעֵת שֶׁהָיָה מוֹהֲרַנַ"ת יָתוֹם אַחֲרֵי אִמּוֹ, שָׁאַל אֶת רַבֵּנוּ זַ"ל בַּמֶּה יוּכַל לַעֲשׂוֹת טוֹבָה לְאִמּוֹ, וְהֵשִׁיב לוֹ, דּוּ זָאלְסְט מַאכִין אֲשֶׁר יָצַר עֶרִינְסְט (תְּבָרֵךְ "אֲשֶׁר יָצַר" בִּרְצִינוּת). וְכִוֵּן לְמַחֲשַׁבְתּוֹ
שֶׁצָּרִיךְ לַעֲשׂוֹת בִּרְכַּת אֲשֶׁר יָצַר:
segments.en: § 3 — R. Nachman Tulshiner Asked Moharan"as Why He Does Not Pass on the Megilas Setarim to R. Yitzchak and R. Efraim; Moharan"as: "I Am Angry at Them — They Are Market People" Once R. Nachman asked Moharan"as z"l: why does he not pass on the Megilas Setarim of our master z"l to his son R. Yitzchak z"l and to Rabbi Efraim the son of Rabbi Naftali z"l? He answered him: Ikh bin oyf zey in broygz — zey zenen mark-mentshn! Zoln nit zayn keyn mark-mentshn — volt zey der Eybershter oykh oysgiführt! [I am angry at them — they are market people! Had they not been market people — the Holy One blessed be He would have also led them forth!]

segments.he:
נח
פַּעַם אַחַת בָּא ר' נַחְמָן מִטּוּלְטְשִׁין אֶל מוֹהֲרַנַ"ת בַּעֲלִיָּתוֹ וְרָאָה שֶׁהוּא כּוֹתֵב, וְלֹא רָצָה לְבַלְבֵּל אוֹתוֹ. וְאַחַר־כָּךְ רָאָה אֶת הַכְּתָב שֶׁל הַתְּפִלָּה "לָמָּה פָּנֶיךָ תַּסְתִּיר" שֶׁהָיָה מָלֵא
דְּמָעוֹת:
segments.en: § 4 — R. Yitzchak z"l Before Entering the Post Office Livelihood Was Very Poor; Wanted to Separate from Worldly Affairs; Moharan"as Refused; His Bitachon Is Only for Himself; After R. Yitzchak Entered the Post — Moharan"as Strengthened Him With Letters R. Yitzchak z"l — before he entered the post office livelihood in Tulchin — was very poor, torn and worn out. And he wanted to separate from worldly affairs for Torah and service — provided his father Moharan"as z"l would look after him and his household. But Moharan"as refused this. From the main thrust of his words about this — it was heard that he said: the bitachon he has is only for himself — and it is difficult for him to find bitachon also for his son. He wanted R. Yitzchak to stand in the trial. But afterwards when he did not stand in the trial and entered the post — from fear lest he fall further, G-d forbid, through worry and longing — on the contrary he strengthened him constantly with letters.

segments.he:
נט
אֶחָד מֵאַנְשֵׁי שְׁלוֹמֵנוּ שֶׁהָיָה סוֹחֵר וְנָסַע עִם סְחוֹרָה, וּבַדֶּרֶךְ נָפַל גֶּשֶׁם. וּפָרַשׂ הָאִישׁ יְרִיעָה (פַּאלָאטְקֶע) אֹהֶל וַיֵּשֶׁב לִלְמֹד. וּבֵין כָּךְ עָבַר מוֹהֲרַנַ"ת זַ"ל וְקָרָא אוֹתוֹ. אַחַר־כָּךְ סִפֵּר מוֹהֲרַנַ"ת שֶׁרָאָה שֶׁהָאִישׁ נֶהֱנָה מְאֹד מֵהַגֶּשֶׁם, שֶׁעַל־יְדֵי כָּךְ יָכוֹל לַעֲבֹד אֶת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ, כִּי בְּוַדַּאי אִי אֶפְשָׁר עַתָּה
לִסְחֹר:
segments.en: § 5 — Said to One Who Praised Livelihood in a Forest Position: "Going Alone in a Forest — One Can Become a Great Proper Jew — or Conversely a Great Scoundrel" The Rav R. Nachman z"l of Tulchin — said to one who greatly praised the livelihood with some forest position [given the great importance of hisbodedus according to the way of our master z"l] — he said about this: Tsu geyen kaséder aleyn in eyn vald — ober men kan vern eyn groyser erlikher Yid — ober farkert — men kan vern eyn groyser holṭay! [To always go alone in a forest — one can become a great proper Jew — or conversely — one can become a great scoundrel!]

segments.he:
ס
מוֹהֲרַנַ"ת הָיָה אוֹמֵר, מִלְחֶמֶת גּוֹג וּמָגוֹג אֵינוֹ נִזְכָּר בִּמְגִלַּת סְתָרִים, מַשְׁמַע שֶׁיִּהְיֶה אֶפִּיקוֹרְסוּת בָּעוֹלָם, וְזֶה יִהְיֶה נִסָּיוֹן
שֶׁלָּנוּ וְשֶׁל מָשִׁיחַ:
segments.en:
§ 6 — One Complained He Could Get Livelihood as a Servant to a Man of Our Fellowship — But That Man Refuses; Moharan"as: "Do You Not Remember — 'And I Have Commanded the Ravens to Feed You'" One complained before R. Nachman mentioned: that it is possible for him to get livelihood as a servant to one of the men of our fellowship — if that man desired him — and since he refuses him — he is compelled to hold this position at the home of a frivolous person — and he therefore does not advance well spiritually in the service of Hashem. He said to him about this: "Why do you not remember — 'And I have commanded the ravens to sustain you'" [I Kings 17:4]? — it was found that Eliyahu's livelihood was specifically through "the ravens."

§ 7 — A Childhood Friend of Moharan"as Who Had Fled From Debts Passed Through Breslov; Moharan"as: "Flee Only to the Almighty" — Go to the House of Study; The Shamash Will Welcome You; Wife and Relatives Came Crying — Be Silent; After Some Days the Whole City Was Stirred; Sympathizers Helped His Wife; Moharan"as Was Told and Was Pleased A friend from the youth of Moharan"as z"l — because he had married a wife in Mogilev — became also a resident of Mogilev. And there he engaged in commerce — and began to conduct his business on a large scale with loans as is the way of merchants. But he did not succeed in his business — and began to go down further and further — until with time he was left naked and destitute — with no way to pay his debts. And therefore from fear and dread of the creditors he became a fugitive — perhaps salvation and deliverance would stand for him in another place — that some livelihood source would be found for him there — and also little by little to pay off the debts. When he fled — his way passed through Breslov. When he came to Breslov he remembered that there he has a dear friend — that is Moharan"as z"l — and therefore turned to him. And since he was a guest — Moharan"as z"l asked him to eat at his home — and asked him about his welfare and situation. And he told him everything that had happened to him. And therefore he found for him the advice — to be a fugitive as is the custom of borrowers who have nothing to repay — and his plan to travel to some place where he has some wealthy relative — and he would stand by him to help in the trouble — to give him some position. Moharan"as z"l said to him: when you come to your relative — your countenance will answer him about your low state. Immediately he will show you signs of displeasure at your coming to him — and also his empty hand he will clench not to give into your hand — and with the saying of "shalom aleikhem" feebly — he will extend to you the tips of his fingers. And perhaps he will give you to eat one or two meals — and regarding a night's lodging I am doubtful whether he will give you at his home. And perhaps also in the house of study there they will not give you a place to sleep — for in a place where they do not know you — there is justification to suspect you of being a thief. And this is no advice at all. And Moharan"as z"l said to him: my advice is — Antlofn nor tsum Eybershtṇ! [Flee only to the Almighty!] That you return to Mogilev — and not to your house — but directly to the house of study. And the main refuge for you will be Torah and prayer — and there everyone knows you that you are not a thief, G-d forbid — and on the contrary — for a respected merchant who stumbled in his business and through circumstances became a debtor and went down and lacks livelihood. And the shamash from the house of study — on the contrary he will receive you with a pleasant countenance and draw you close in every kind of closeness. And after some days — your wife and her relatives will come to visit you with their cries and arguments that were heard — and you shall not answer them anything — only the one answer shall be for you: silence. And with this I am confident that Hashem will be with you in your help before long. These words that came from the heart of a righteous faithful friend entered the heart of his friend — and so he did. And from Breslov he returned to Mogilev — and straight to the house of study — on Torah and service. And everything was exactly as Moharan"as z"l had told him. The shamash received him with a pleasant face and drew him close in every kind of closeness. And after some days — his wife and her relatives came to visit him with their cries and arguments — and he was firm: "Silence is beautiful." Some more days passed — and the whole city was in a stir over this matter. Until several of his acquaintances and friends were aroused to have mercy on him and on his household — and to create a livelihood situation for him — and they gathered a sum of money and established for his wife a market stall with a little merchandise. And Hashem was with him — and his wife began little by little to succeed. And he too sometimes came out from the house of study to help her — until the business grew and grew — until she became an industrious wife providing all the livelihood in comfort — and also paying off the debts. And he sometimes came out to help her a little and to review the account books. And therefore he wrote to Moharan"as z"l all of this. And happy is he — who merited that through him such great merit was brought about.

segments.he:
סא
פַּעַם אַחַת שָׁלַח רַב אֶחָד לְר' נְתַנְאֵל טֶעפְּלִיקֶער שֶׁלֹּא יִתֵּן לְמוֹהֲרַנַ"ת לְהִתְאַכְסֵן אֶצְלוֹ כְּשֶׁיָּבוֹא לְטֶעפְּלִיק. וְהֵשִׁיב לוֹ: זֶה אִי אֶפְשָׁר, שֶׁמּוֹהַרְנַ"ת אֵין לוֹ שׁוּם מָקוֹם לְהִתְאַכְסֵן כִּי אִם אֶצְלִי, וּמַה שֶּׁהָרַב מַפְחִיד אוֹתִי מָה אוּכַל לַעֲשׂוֹת. וְכֵן הָיָה. וְר' נְתַנְאֵל יָרֵא שֶׁמָּא יִשְׁמַע מוֹהֲרַנַ"ת מִן הַמִּכְתָּב הַנַּ"ל, עַל־כֵּן שָׁלַח מִכְתָּב לְמוֹהֲרַנַ"ת זַ"ל שֶׁאֵינוֹ שׁוֹמֵעַ לְדִבְרֵי הָרַב הַנַּ"ל כְּלָל. וְאַחַר־כָּךְ כְּשֶׁבָּא מוֹהֲרַנַ"ת לְטֶעפְּלִיק נִתְאַכְסֵן בְּבֵית רַבִּי נְתַנְאֵל בְּכָבוֹד גָּדוֹל, וְעָשָׂה סְעֻדָּה גְּדוֹלָה עֲבוּרוֹ, וּבִתּוֹ נִזְדָּרְזָה וְעָשְׂתָה טֵייגְלִיךְ (כְּמִין מַאֲכָל בָּצֵק מְטֻגָּן) לִכְבוֹד מוֹהֲרַנַ"ת. אַחַר־כָּךְ רָאָה מוֹהֲרַנַ"ת שֶׁיֵּשׁ לְרַבִּי נְתַנְאֵל קְצָת גַּדְלוּת, אָמַר לוֹ מוֹהֲרַנַ"ת אֶפְשָׁר מֵיינְסְטוּ אַז אָן דִּיר וָואלְט אִיךְ קֵיין סְטַאנְצִיֶע נִיט גִּיהַאט, אִיךְ אָהן דִּיר קָאן זִיךְ בַּאגֶעהְן, דּוּא אָהְן מִיר נִיט (אוּלַי אַתָּה חוֹשֵׁב שֶׁבִּלְעָדֶיךָ לֹא הָיָה לִי אַכְסַנְיָא, אֲנִי בִּלְעָדֶיךָ אֶסְתַּדֵּר, אַתָּה בִּלְעָדִי לֹא). אַחַר־כָּךְ שָׁמַע הָרַב הַנַּ"ל הַדָּבָר הַזֶּה, וְאָמַר שֶׁבִּשְׁבִיל הַדָּבָר הַזֶּה לֹא יִהְיֶה לָהּ בָּנִים לְבַת הָר' נְתַנְאֵל, וַתֹּאמֶר מָה אֲנִי יְכוֹלָה לַעֲשׂוֹת. אַחַר־כָּךְ אָמַר מוֹהֲרַנַ"ת לְר' נְתַנְאֵל, עַתָּה פָּתַח הָרַב אֶת פִּי לְהִתְפַּלֵּל עָלֶיהָ לְהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ, וְנִפְקְדָה בְּבֵן זָכָר. וְר' נְתַנְאֵל הָיָה מְקֹרָב לְרַבֵּנוּ זַ"ל, וּפַעַם אַחַת נָתַן לְרַבֵּנוּ זַ"ל עֲשָׂרָה אֲדֻמִּים וְשִׁבַּח אוֹתוֹ רַבֵּנוּ זַ"ל וְאָמַר שֶׁמֵּעוֹלָם לֹא הָיָה לוֹ כְּמוֹ כֵן. וְאָמַר שֶׁהוּא אוֹהֵב אֶת הָרֶענְדְלִיךְ שֶׁל הָר' נְתַנְאֵל, מִפְּנֵי שֶׁהָיָה קַמְצָן גָּדוֹל, וְזֶה הָיָה אֶצְלוֹ מְסִירוּת נֶפֶשׁ לָכֹף אֶת יִצְרוֹ. פַּעַם אַחַת הִבְטִיחַ לִתֵּן לְמוֹהֲרַנַ"ת שְׁנֵים עָשָׂר רוּבָּל כֶּסֶף עַל בִּנְיַן הַקְּלוֹיְז, וְנָתַן לוֹ מִתְּחִלָּה שְׁלֹשָׁה רוּבָּל כֶּסֶף, וְאַחַר־כָּךְ נָתַן לוֹ עוֹד הַפַּעַם שְׁלֹשָׁה רוּבָּל כֶּסֶף, עַד שֶׁנָּתַן הַכֹּל בְּכַמָּה פְּעָמִים. וּכְשֶׁנֶּחֱלָה ר' נְתַנְאֵל בָּא אֶצְלוֹ ר' נָתָן, אָמַר לוֹ ר' נְתַנְאֵל לְר' נָתָן קַיְּימוּ בִּי הַגְּמָרָא 'יָהִיב לֵהּ יְדֵהּ' וְכוּ'. אָמַר לוֹ מוֹהֲרַנַ"ת לָאו כָּל אָדָם יָכוֹל לַעֲשׂוֹת אֶת הַדָּבָר הַזֶּה. אָמַר לוֹ רַבִּי נְתַנְאֵל אֲנִי מַאֲמִין שֶׁאַתֶּם יְכוֹלִין לַעֲשׂוֹת זֹאת, אָמַר לוֹ מוֹהֲרַנַ"ת לֹא בְּכָל אָדָם יְכוֹלִין לַעֲשׂוֹת אֶת הַדָּבָר הַזֶּה. אַחַר־כָּךְ הָלַךְ מֵאִתּוֹ מוֹהֲרַנַ"ת, וַיֵּלֶךְ דֶּרֶךְ הַקֶּעךְ (הַמִּטְבָּח). וַיֹּאמֶר לְבִתּוֹ שֶׁל ר' נְתַנְאֵל אִם יִתֵּן ר' נְתַנְאֵל אֶת הַצְּדָקָה יוֹתֵר מִכְּפִי יְכָלְתּוֹ, אֶפְשָׁר שֶׁיִּחְיֶה עוֹד. אָמְרָה לוֹ אֵלֵךְ וְאֹמַר זֹאת לְאָבִי, אָמַר לָהּ מוֹהֲרַנַ"ת אִיךְ וִויל עֶהר זָאל זִיךְ אַלֵיין אָנְשְׁטוֹיְסֶען (אַנִי רוֹצֶה שֶׁהוּא יִתְאַמֵּץ מֵעַצְּמוֹ). וּפַעַם אַחַת הָיָה מוֹהֲרַנַ"ת בְּיַחַד עִם הָרַב הַנַּ"ל וְדִבֵּר הָרַב הַנַּ"ל מֵהַקַּמְצָנוּת שֶׁל ר' נְתַנְאֵל, וְסִפֵּר אָז שֶׁפּוֹסֵק אֶחָד לֹא נִפְסְקָה הֲלָכָה כְּמוֹתוֹ, מִפְּנֵי שֶׁהָיָה קַמְצָן. וְזֶה הַדָּבָר הָיָה בְּסוֹד לִיחִידֵי הַדּוֹרוֹת, וְנִעֲנַע ר' נָתָן בְּרֹאשׁוֹ כְּאִלּוּ יוֹדֵעַ. וְכָפַף הָרַב הַנַּ"ל רֹאשׁוֹ לְמוֹהֲרַנַ"ת שֶׁיֹּאמַר לוֹ, וְאָמַר לוֹ, וְנִתְפַּעֵל הָרַב הַנַּ"ל וְאָמַר לְמוֹהֲרַנַ"ת הֲלֹא בְּוַדַּאי הֲיִיתֶם צְרִיכִים לֵילֵךְ בְּבִגְדֵי מֶשִׁי. וְהֵשִׁיב לוֹ
מוֹהֲרַנַ"ת זֹאת גַּם־כֵּן חַיָּב ר' נְתַנְאֵל:
segments.en: § 8 — Akiva the Teacher in Tulchin — Versed in Philosophy and Heresy; Composed a Book of Mockery; Came to Moharan"as Intending to Mock; Moharan"as Said Torah About Recognizing a Deceiver; Akiva Left Without Mocking — and Praised Moharan"as; Through This R. Tsvi Pesach Was Drawn Close; Akiva Later Joined a Different Rebbe; R. Tsvi Pesach's Story In Tulchin there was one — Akiva the teacher. And he was expert in the Talmud and Decisors — worthy of rendering decisions — and also expert in the books of truth and the books of Tzadikim. But also expert in books of philosophy, inquiry, and heresy — to the extent that he composed some book of mockery about the Tzadikim of the generation. But he was like one of the G-d-fearing — with a beard and long sidelocks. And among his townsfolk he was considered a learned G-d-fearer. Once he was in Breslov — and entered Moharan"as z"tl — in order to mock everything he would see and hear at his home. And therefore he asked first of all from Moharan"as z"l that he say him a word of Torah. And then he said to him in the name of our master z"l the small passage in Likutay Moharan about how the Tzadik examines the one who comes to him to find his lost object — if he is a deceiver — as is written "until your brother's seeking" [ad drosh akhikha — Deuteronomy 22:2] — him. When Akiva heard this — and knew how far the words of Moharan"as z"l reached — when he left Moharan"as z"l — not only did he not mock anymore — on the contrary — he recounted several times to people this occurrence and praised Moharan"as z"l. And this is Akiva the teacher who taught R. Tsvi Pesach z"l of Tulchin — the son-in-law of R. Nachman Tulshiner z"l — through whom specifically R. Tsvi mentioned drew close to the men of our fellowship. For once — still while being his student — he said to his teacher Akiva mentioned: with what you do not believe in the Baal Shem Tov z"l — in this I am not of one view with you — and I believe in the Baal Shem Tov z"l. In this however I am undecided — to which group of Chassidim to draw close — and therefore I ask you: what is your view on this? He answered him: if one is to draw close to a group of Chassidim — the finest group is the group of "the Breslovers." From then on R. Tsvi mentioned drew close to the men of our fellowship — and merited to become the son-in-law of R. Nachman Tulshiner — the disciple and attendant of Moharan"as z"l — and merited that through him some of the books of our master z"l and Moharan"as z"l were printed in the Land of Israel and outside the Land. In his youth he was in the Land [of Israel] and returned to outside the Land — and in his old age returned again to the Land — and lived about a year. And in the year 5670 he passed away here in Jerusalem — may it be built and established speedily in our days — Amen. May his soul be bound in the bond of life. Akiva mentioned — from want of livelihood — drew close to the Rav Davidl of Talna — and asked him for some rabbinical position — and he gave him the city of Dobaveh near Uman.

segments.he:
סב
תּוֹרָה א' מָצָא מוֹהֲרַנַ"ת אַחַר הַדְפָּסָה הָרִאשׁוֹנָה בְּסִגְנוֹן אַחֵר, לֹא כְּמוֹ שֶׁנִּדְפַּס בַּהַדְפָּסָה הָרִאשׁוֹנָה, וְנִרְאָה לוֹ מַה שֶּׁמָּצָא אַחַר־כָּךְ. וְעַל־כֵּן כְּשֶׁהִדְפִּיס הַסִּפּוּרֵי מַעֲשִׂיּוֹת וְאַחַר־כָּךְ הִדְפִּיס אֶת הַתּוֹרָה א' אֵצֶל הַסִּפּוּרֵי מַעֲשִׂיּוֹת, וְאַחַר־כָּךְ הִדְפִּיס אוֹתָהּ בְּלֶעמְבֶּרְג כְּמוֹ שֶׁנִּדְפַּס עַכְשָׁו. רַב אֶחָד הָיָה לוֹ קִנְאָה עַל רַבֵּנוּ זַ"ל עַל שֶׁהַמַּגִּיד מִטִירָאוִויצֶע נוֹסֵעַ אֵלָיו, וְהָיָה רָגִיל לִשְׁלֹחַ אֲנָשִׁים לְהַמַּגִּיד וְדִבְּרוּ מַלְשִׁינוּת עַל רַבֵּנוּ זַ"ל וְכוּ'. וְהָלַךְ הַמַּגִּיד אֵצֶל חֹתְנוֹ ר' יִצְחָק, שֶׁהָיָה מְקֹרָב לְרַבֵּנוּ זַ"ל, וְשָׁאַל אוֹתוֹ אִם יֵשׁ לוֹ כְּתָבִים מֵרַבֵּנוּ זַ"ל. וְהֶרְאָה לוֹ הַתּוֹרָה ב' אֱמֹר אֶל הַכֹּהֲנִים. וְנִתְפַּעֵל הַמַּגִּיד מְאֹד וְאָמַר מָה אֹמַר עַל הַתּוֹרָה שֶׁהוּא זֹהַר, הֵם גְּבוֹהִים מִזֹּהַר. הֵם תִּקּוּנִים הֵם גְּבוֹהִים מִתִּקּוּנִים. וּבִזָּה מְאֹד הַמַּלְשִׁינִים הַנַּ"ל. אֶחָד שָׁאַל לְמוֹהֲרַנַ"ת מִי גָּדוֹל. הַקָּטָן שֶׁמְּקֹרָב לְצַדִּיק, אוֹ הַגָּדוֹל שֶׁאֵינוֹ מְקֹרָב, אָמַר לוֹ הֲלֹא בִּימֵי מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּנוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם, שֶׁאִם אֶחָד הָיָה עוֹשֶׂה דָּבָר גָּדוֹל לְהַמִּשְׁכָּן וְלֹא הֱבִיאוֹ לְמֹשֶׁה רַבֵּנוּ בְּוַדַּאי לֹא הָיָה שׁוּם חֲשִׁיבוּת כְּלָל, אֲבָל מִי שֶׁעָשָׂה דָּבָר קָטָן וֶהֱבִיאוֹ אֶל מֹשֶׁה בְּוַדַּאי הָיָה חָשׁוּב מְאֹד. וְאָמַר אָז הַתּוֹרָה ב' הַנַּ"ל, שֶׁדַּיְקָא מֹשֶׁה יוּכַל לְעַיְלָא שְׁיָיפָא בִּשְׁיָיפָא (שֶׁאֵין שׁוּם אֶחָד מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל יָכוֹל
לְאַעֲלָא שַׁיְפָא בְּשַׁיְפָא כָּל חַד לְדוּכְתֵּיהּ אֶלָּא משֶׁה בִּלְחוּד):
segments.en: § 9 — Moharan"as Said to One: "When You Sit With a Woman and Tell Me You Are a Proper Jew — I Will Believe You — But Not Without Sitting With a Woman"; Also R. Nakhmanleh's Grandson Once Moharan"as z"l said to one: Az du vest zitsn mit eyn isha — un du vest mir zogn az du bist eyn erlikher Yid — vel ikh dir gloybn! Ober nit zitsn mit a isha — un du vest mir zogn du bist eyn herlikher Yid — vel ikh dir gor nit gloybn! [When you sit with a woman and tell me you are a proper Jew — I will believe you! But without sitting with a woman — and you tell me you are an excellent Jew — I will not believe you at all!] And likewise his grandson R. Mikhleli z"l of Tulchin said to one who was living without a wife: Du bist dokh nisht keyn guter! [You are not good after all!] The Torah testifies: "It is not good for man to be alone."

segments.he:
סג
פַּעַם אַחַת סִפְּרוּ לְמוֹהֲרַנַ"ת שֶׁר' נַפְתָּלִי הוּא כַּעֲסָן. וְאָמַר מוֹהֲרַנַ"ת לֹא יָדַעְתִּי שֶׁהוּא גָּדוֹל כָּל־כָּךְ, שֶׁעַל כָּל אֵלֶּה הוּא ר' נַפְתָּלִי, שֶׁהַבַּעַל דָּבָר אֵינוֹ יָכוֹל לְהַפִּילוֹ עַל־יְדֵי כַּעַס. וּפַעַם אַחַת הָיוּ מְסַפְּרִים אֵיזֶה אֲנָשִׁים זֶה עַל זֶה, וְשָׁאַל אֶחָד אֶת הַשֵּׁנִי מִפְּנֵי מָה עָשָׂה הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ גְּזֵרוֹת נֶעקְרֶעטִין פֹּה בְּרוּסְיָא, בִּשְׁלָמָא בְּקִירָ"ה הָיָה עֹנֶשׁ הַזֶּה מִפְּנֵי שֶׁקָּרְעוּ אֶת סִפְרֵי הַתּוֹלְדוֹת זַ"ל. וְהֵשִׁיב הַשֵּׁנִי אֶפְשָׁר מִפְּנֵי שֶׁקָּרְעוּ סִפְרֵי ר' נַחְמָן מִבְּרַסְלֶב. וְר' נַפְתָּלִי סִפֵּר מִזֶּה וְאָמַר, מִפְּנֵי שֶׁהָעוֹלָם הָיוּ חוֹלְקִים עַל הָאֲרִ"י הַקָּדוֹשׁ נִגְזַר עַל הָעוֹלָם גְּזֵרַת ת"ח. וּמִפְּנֵי שֶׁהָיוּ מִתְנַגְּדִים עַל הַבַּעַל שֵׁם טוֹב זַ"ל נִגְזַר עַל הָעוֹלָם גְּזֵרַת גַאנְטִי (שֶׁהָיָה אַחַר פְּטִירַת הַבַּעַל שֵׁם טוֹב בִּשְׁנַת תק"ך). וּבִשְׁבִיל שֶׁהָיָה הִתְנַגְּדוּת עַל רַבֵּנוּ זַ"ל, נִגְזַר עַל הָעוֹלָם גְּזֵרַת נֶעקְרֶעטִין וְכָל הַגְּזֵרוֹת עַד בִּיאַת מְשִׁיחַ צִדְקֵנוּ בִּמְהֵרָה בְּיָמֵינוּ אָמֵן. וּפַעַם אַחַת סִפֵּר רַבֵּנוּ זַ"ל, רָאִיתִי בָּעוֹלָם הָעֶלְיוֹן שֶׁמִּתְפַּלֵּל אֶחָד אֵיזֶה תְּפִלָּה וְכוּ' (וְשִׁבַּח מְאֹד אֶת הַתְּפִלָּה) הָאבּ אִיךְ אוֹיף גִּידֶעקְט דָּאס פָּנִים הָאבּ אִיךְ גִּיזֶעהן אַז דָּאס אִיז מַיין נַפְתָּלִי (גִּלִּיתִי אֶת פָּנָיו וְרָאִיתִי שֶׁזֶּה נַפְתָּלִי שֶׁלִּי). וּפַעַם אַחַת הָיָה מַעֲשֶׂה בְּעֵת הַנֶּעקְרִיטִין שֶׁהַדֶּרֶךְ הָיָה אֲפִלּוּ מִי שֶׁהָיָה לוֹ בִּילֶעט חֵרוּת (תְּעוּדַת שִׁחְרוּר), הָיוּ מְחַפְּשִׂין וְלוֹקְחִים הַבִּילֶעט וְקוֹרְעִים אוֹתוֹ וּמַעֲלִילִים שֶׁאֵין לוֹ בִּילֶעט, כְּדֵי לִקַּח אוֹתוֹ לְאִישׁ חַיִל. וְהָיָה אֶחָד שֶׁהִשְׂכִּיר אֶת בְּנוֹ שֶׁיִּהְיֶה אֵצֶל ר' נַפְתָּלִי. וּפַעַם אַחַת בָּאוּ אֵצֶל רַבִּי נַפְתָּלִי וּמָצְאוּ אֶת הַבָּחוּר וְשָׁאֲלוּ בִּילֶעט. וַיִּירָא אָבִיו שֶׁיִּקְרְעוּ הַבִּילֶעט, עַל־כֵּן עָשָׂה קוֹלוֹת עַד שֶׁהִתְקַבְּצוּ כָּל הָעִיר, וְאָז לֹא יָרֵא עוֹד לְהַרְאוֹת הַבִּילֶעט כִּי כֻּלָּם יִהְיוּ עֵדִים. וְרַבִּי נַפְתָּלִי הִתְפַּלֵּל אָז מִנְחָה, וַיִּירָא הָאִישׁ הַנַּ"ל שֶׁרַבִּי נַפְתָּלִי לֹא יַקְפִּיד עַל שֶׁבִּלְבְּלוֹ מִתְּפִלָּתוֹ. וּבִשְׁעַת הַסְּעֻדָּה בִּקֵּשׁ מִמֶּנּוּ שֶׁיִּמְחֹל לוֹ. וְרַבִּי נַפְתָּלִי הֵשִׁיב לוֹ שֶׁאֵינוֹ יוֹדֵע כְּלָל מִכָּל הַמַּעֲשֶׂה, כִּי תְּפִלָּתוֹ הָיְתָה בְּהִתְפַּשְּׁטוּת הַגַּשְׁמִיּוּת, עַד
שֶׁהָרַעַשׁ מִכָּל הָעִיר שֶׁהָיָה בְּבֵיתוֹ וְהוּא לֹא שָׁמַע כְּלָל:
segments.en: § 10 — Moharan"as Said to One: "I Believe — Happy Is the Man Who Hearkens to Your Commandments — and If You Are This — Happy Are You" Once Moharan"as z"l said to one: Ikh gloyb az — "Ashrei Ish Sheshoma'a LeMitsvosekha" — un oyb du bist dos — voyl iz dir! [I believe that — "Happy is the man who hearkens to Your commandments" — and if you are this — happy are you!]

segments.he:
סד
פַּעַם בִּשְׁעַת דָּחֳקוֹ שֶׁל מוֹהֲרַנַ"ת הָיָה שֶׁהִגִּיעַ יָרִיד הָאַחֲרוֹן שֶׁל עֶרֶב פֶּסַח וְעוֹד לֹא הָיָה לוֹ צָרְכֵי פֶּסַח. וּבְכֵן בַּהַשְׁכָּמָה יוֹם זֶה עוֹד קֹדֶם הַתְּפִלָּה הִתְחִילָה זוּגָתוֹ דִּישֶׁעל עָלֶיהָ הַשָּׁלוֹם לְהִתְאוֹנֵן לְפָנָיו עַל זֶה, בְּהַצָּעוֹת טַעֲנוֹתֶיהָ הַנִּשְׁמָעוֹת לוֹ וּמַדְאִיבִים אֶת נַפְשׁוֹ כָּל־כָּךְ עַד שֶׁעַל זֶה הֵעִיד וְאָמַר אַחַר־כָּךְ לִפְנֵי אַנְשֵׁי שְׁלוֹמֵנוּ אוֹי הָאט זִיא מִיט מִיר אָבְּגִלֶערִינְט אַ פֶּרֶק פוּן מָרָה שְׁחוֹרָה (אוֹי הִיא לִמְּדָה אוֹתִי פֶּרֶק בְּמָרָה שְׁחוֹרָה). בְּכָל זֹאת כְּשֶׁהִגִּיעַ זְמַן הַתְּפִלָּה חִזֵּק אֶת עַצְמוֹ בְּכָל מִינֵי הִתְחַזְּקוּת בְּכָל עֹז וְתַעֲצוּמוֹת בֶּאֱמוּנָה וּבִטָּחוֹן לְדַבֵּק אֶת עַצְמוֹ בְּהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ, וְהִתְפַּלֵּל תְּפִלָּתוֹ עַד שֶׁאַחַר הַתְּפִלָּה הֵעִיד הָר' נַחְמָן טוּלְטְשִׁינֶער עָלָיו שֶׁרָאָה אוֹתוֹ בְּפָנִים צְהֻבּוֹת וּשְׂמֵחִים כְּמוֹ שֶׁנִּתְמַלֵּא חֶסְרוֹנוֹ. וְכֵן בְּיוֹם זֶה הָיָה יוֹמָא דְּשׁוּקָא בִּבְרַסְלֶב, שֶׁדֶּרֶךְ אַנְשֵׁי רָארִיד סָמוּךְ לִבְרַסְלֶב הִיא לָבוֹא לְשָׁמָּה עַל הַיָּרִיד. וּבָאוּ אֵלָיו שְׁנַיִם אוֹ שְׁלֹשָׁה אֲנָשִׁים מֵאַנְשֵׁי שְׁלוֹמֵנוּ וְנָתְנוּ לוֹ סְכוּם הָגוּן וְנִתְמַלֵּא חֶסְרוֹנוֹ בַּכֹּל מִכֹּל כֹּל. וְהַשָּׁעָה שֶׁנָּתְנוּ לוֹ אָמַר הָר' נַחְמָן הַנַּ"ל שֶׁלֹּא רָאָה בְּפָנָיו שׁוּם שִׁנּוּי שֶׁל שִׂמְחָה יְתֵרָה, בִּשְׁבִיל שֶׁעוֹד קֹדֶם שֶׁבָּאוּ הָיָה מָלֵא בְּבִטָּחוֹן חָזָק בְּהִתְמַלְּאוּת הַחֶסְרוֹן כְּמֻנָּח בְּכִיסוֹ, וְאַךְ אֲנָשִׁים אֵלּוּ זָכוּ לִהְיוֹת הַשְּׁלוּחִים
לְמִצְוָה רַבָּה זוֹ.
בְּטוּלְטְשִׁין הָיָה אֶחָד הָר' יוֹסִיל הוֹיזְנֶער שֶׁזָּכָה לִשְׁבּוֹת שַׁבָּת אֶחָד אֵצֶל רַבֵּנוּ זַ"ל, וְהוּא הָיָה גַּם מְעַט מְלֻמָּד בְּשָׂפָה רוּסִית וְחָשׁוּב גַּם אֵצֶל שָׂרִים. וּבְכֵן הָיָה מִנִּכְבְּדֵי הָעִיר בַּעַל דֵּעָה וּדְבָרָיו נִשְׁמָעִים, וְעַל־פִּיו נִתְמַנָּה הָר' יִצְחָק בֶּן מוֹהֲרַנַ"ת זַ"ל לִמְנַהֵל בְּהַפָּאסְט (הַדֹּאַר) בְּטוּלְטְשִׁין. אַחַר־כָּךְ כְּשֶׁנִּתְגַּבֵּר הַמַּחֲלֹקֶת עַל אַנְשֵׁי שְׁלוֹמֵנוּ. וּלְהַמִּתְנַגְּדִים הֻתַּר לַעֲשׂוֹת לְאַנְשֵׁי שְׁלוֹמֵנוּ כָּל מַה שֶּׁלִּבָּם חָפֵץ. וְכָל מִי שֶׁלֹּא קִלֵּל אֶת מוֹהֲרַנַ"ת זַ"ל סִימָן שֶׁהוּא גַּם־כֵּן בְּרֶסְלֶבֶר וּמֻתָּר לְקַפֵּחַ פַּרְנָסָתוֹ. וּבְכֵן הֵחֵלּוּ הַמִּתְנַגְּדִים לְדַבֵּר עַל לֵב הָרַב ר' יוֹסִיל הַנַּ"ל שֶׁיְּקַפַּח גַּם אֶת פַּרְנָסַת ר' יִצְחָק הַנַּ"ל שֶׁהוּא נוֹסֵעַ לְאָבִיו לִבְרַסְלֶב. וְהָר' יוֹסִיל הַנַּ"ל דָּחָה אוֹתָם בָּזֶה וְכִי בִּשְׁבִיל שֶׁנּוֹסֵעַ הוּא לִבְרַסְלֶב לְאָבִיו הוּא אוֹת שֶׁהוּא בְּרֶסְלֶבֶר אֵין מִזֶּה רְאָיָה, הוּא סְתָם נוֹסֵעַ לְכָבוֹד אֵלָיו, וְהַמִּתְנַגְּדִים הֻכְרְחוּ לְקַבֵּל דְּבָרָיו. אָמְנָם כְּשֶׁהִגִּיעַ הַזְּמַן לִנְסֹעַ לְאוּמַן עַל רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה אָז הָיָה בֶּאֱמֶת הָר' יִצְחָק הַנַּ"ל בִּמְצוּקָה, בְּאִם יִסַּע לְשָׁמָּה אָז יִהְיֶה הוֹכָחָה גְּדוֹלָה שֶׁהוּא בְּרֶסְלֶבֶר וּבְכֵן הִקְדִּים לִנְסֹעַ לְאָבִיו מוֹהֲרַנַ"ת זַ"ל לִשְׁאֹל אֶת פִּיו מַה יַּעֲשֶׂה עַכְשָׁו עַל זֶה אָמַר לוֹ אָבִיו שֶׁהַנְּסִיעָה לְאוּמַן עַל רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה זֶה עוֹלֶה עַל הַכֹּל וּמְחֻיָּבִין זֹאת לְקַיֵּם בִּמְסִירוּת נֶפֶשׁ. מוּבָן שֶׁלֹּא הִשְׁגִּיחַ עַל שׁוּם דָּבָר, וְעַל רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה נָסַע לְאוּמַן. עָבַר הָרֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה הֵבִין הָר' יִצְחָק הַנַּ"ל שֶׁלַּחֲזֹר לְבֵיתוֹ אִי אֶפְשָׁר לוֹ הֲלֹא עַכְשָׁו בְּוַדַּאי הוּא מְחֻסַּר פַּרְנָסָה. וְאִשְׁתּוֹ הַשְּׁנִיָּה גַּם־כֵּן הָיְתָה מִצַּד הַמִּתְנַגְּדִים (שֶׁעָלֶיהָ אָמַר מוֹהֲרַנַ"ת אִלּוּ לֹא הָיָה כְּבָר מְגֹרָשׁ מֵאִשָּׁה הָרִאשׁוֹנָה, הָיָה מְצַוֶּה עָלָיו לְגָרְשָׁהּ), וְעַכְשָׁו עוֹד לָהּ טַעֲנָה הַנִּשְׁמַעַת "פַּרְנָסָה" אִם כֵּן עָלָיו לִהְיוֹת נָע וָנָד בֵּין אַנְשֵׁי שְׁלוֹמֵנוּ וְלִהְיוֹת פָּרוּשׁ מֵעִסְקֵי הָעוֹלָם הַזֶּה לְגַמְרֵי, רַק זֹאת לֹא יָדַע לְאָן יַעֲשֶׂה דַּרְכּוֹ רִאשׁוֹנָה. וּבְכֵן בָּא לְאָבִיו זַ"ל לִשְׁפֹּךְ לְפָנָיו אֶת מְרִירוּת לְבָבוֹ, וּלְבַסּוֹף שָׁאַל אוֹתוֹ לְאֵיזֶה מָקוֹם לִנְסֹעַ בְּזוֹ הָרֶגַע. מוֹהֲרַנַ"ת זַצַ"ל בְּגֹדֶל חָכְמָתוֹ וְצִדְקָתוֹ הֵבִין אַחֶרֶת, וְאָמַר לוֹ אַדְּרַבָּא! שׁוּב לְבֵיתְךָ לְטוּלְטְשִׁין וְיָשָׁר לְבֵיתְךָ, וְאִשְׁתְּךָ כִּי תִּפְעֹר פִּיהָ בְּטַעֲנוֹתֶיהָ וְצַעֲקוֹתֶיהָ, אַתָּה לֹא תַּעֲנֶה דָּבָר אַךְ תִּשְׁתֹּק. כְּשֶׁתַּפְרִיעַ לְךָ מֵאֵיזֶה עֵסֶק שֶׁתַּעֲסֹק בְּבֵיתְךָ אַל תִּפְחַד מִמֶּנָּה לַעֲזֹב אֶת הָעֵסֶק. תֹּאמַר לָהּ בְּעַזּוּת שֶׁאַתָּה בַּעַל הַבַּיִת. כִּי תָּרִים יָד לְהַכּוֹתְךָ אַתָּה תָּרֵם מַטְּךָ. בְּקִצּוּר אֲמָרִים אַל תִּירָא מִמֶּנָּה כְּלָל וּכְלָל. וְאִם אוֹדוֹת פַּרְנָסָה ה' רַב לְהוֹשִׁיעַ. וּבְכֵן מִהֵר הָר' יִצְחָק הַנַּ"ל לְקַיֵּם אֶת דִּבְרֵי אָבִיו וְחָזַר לְטוּלְטְשִׁין וְיָשָׁר לְבֵיתוֹ. וְשָׁם הַכֹּל כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמַר לוֹ אָבִיו זַ"ל, אִשְׁתּוֹ הֵחֵלָּה לִצְעֹק וְהוּא שׁוֹתֵק. מַפְרִיעָה הִיא אוֹתוֹ מֵאֵיזֶה עֵסֶק שֶׁעָסַק, וְהוּא עוֹשֶׂה אֶת שֶׁלּוֹ. "אֲנִי בַּעַל הַבַּיִת", מְנַסָּה הִיא לְהָרִים אֶת יָדָהּ עָלָיו, וְהוּא הִקְדִּים נֶגְדָּהּ עִם הַקָאטְשֶׁערֶע (מִין מוֹט). וּמִפַּרְנָסַת הַפָּאסְט כַּמּוּבָן הִסִּיחַ דַּעְתּוֹ. לְמָחֳרָתוֹ בְּדֶרֶךְ הִלּוּכוֹ בִּרְחוֹב הָעִיר, נִפְגַּשׁ עִם הָר' יוֹסִיל הַנַּ"ל שֶׁזָּכָה לִשְׁבּוֹת שַׁבָּת אֶחָד אֵצֶל רַבֵּנוּ זַ"ל. וּבְכֵן אַדְּרַבָּה הוּא הִתְחִיל לְדַבֵּר עִם הָר' יִצְחָק וְשָׁאַל אוֹתוֹ בְּתֵמַהּ, מַדּוּעַ אֵינְךָ בָּא אֶל הַפָּאסְט? אַל תִּירָא וְאַל תֵּחָת, שׁוּב אֶל הַפָּאסְט וְהַכֹּל כְּמִקֹּדֶם. כְּשֶׁהִגִּיעַ עֶרֶב יוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים, מֵאֵימַת יוֹם הַדִּין שֶׁהָיְתָה בֶּאֱמֶת בַּדּוֹרוֹת הַקּוֹדְמִים עַל כָּל זֶרַע יִשְׂרָאֵל מִקָּטָן וְעַד גָּדוֹל, אִשְׁתּוֹ גַּם־כֵּן עָשְׂתָה כָּזֹאת, וּפִיְּסָה אֶת בַּעְלָהּ הָר' יִצְחָק זַ"ל, וְהַכֹּל לוֹ שָׁלוֹם כְּקֶדֶם. מִהֵר הַבֵּן יַקִּיר זֶה לְהוֹדִיעַ כָּל זֹאת לְאָבִיו. אָז אָמַר מוֹהֲרַנַ"ת זַ"ל עַל דֶּרֶךְ הֲלָצָה אֵיין הַצְלָחָה פַאר אַנְשֵׁי שְׁלוֹמֵנוּ, וָואס יוֹם כִּפּוּר גֶּעפַאלְט תָּמִיד בַּאלְד נָאךְ רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה הַצְלָחָה לְאַנְשֵׁי
שְׁלוֹמֵנוּ שֶׁיּוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים חָל תָּמִיד תֵּכֶף אַחַר רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה:
segments.en:
§ 11 — At His Uncle R. Yudil in Heysin; After a Long Discussion Moharan"as Concluded: "This World Is Not — and Cannot Be Obtained; Torah and Service Is Yes — and Can Indeed Be Obtained"; Young R. Nachman Heard This and Resolved to Cleave to Moharan"as; The Full Story of His Drawing Close At the home of the uncle of R. Nachman Tulshiner — R. Yudil the brother of his father — in Heysin — after a long discussion of Moharan"as z"l with the men of our fellowship about the purpose — he said the conclusion: Di velt iz nisht — un men ken zi nit bekumen. Toyre un avoyde iz yo — un men ken dos yo bekumen! [This world is not — and it cannot be obtained. Torah and service is yes — and it can indeed be obtained!] And this R. Nachman mentioned heard when he was a boy — and was greatly moved by this conclusion — to the extent that for him it became a conclusion to always be attached and close to Moharan"as z"l. [There is more to write about the unfolding of the drawing close of R. Nachman mentioned.] And this is the order of the unfolding of the drawing close of R. Nachman Tulshiner z"l: his grandfather R. Yitzchak was of the men of our master z"l and a distinguished scholar. And therefore our master z"l once said to him: "You are a scholar — and therefore I will tell you a scholarly pilpul." And he told him the explanation in Likutay Moharan on the verse "And all the people answered etc. and Moshe returned the words of the people" etc. His son R. Avrohom [after whom R. Avrohom z"tl is named] was also close to the men of our fellowship — but not so much — and his first wife when she passed away left him two small orphans — a girl and a boy — he is R. Nachman Tulshiner — and he married a second wife. Shortly after that — he too passed away [and then R.
